- **One active World per project.** A project can hold several Robot Worlds, but while one is active, the others cannot be activated (*Another Robot World is already running in this project*).
- **Active Stations connect automatically** to the project's active World, including their camera and IMU gateways. A Station activated before the World connects once the World is up.
- **Robots are matched by name.** A simulation gateway drives the robot named in its gateway document (**Robot name**): the name of the robot's articulation prim in the World, for example `jackal`. Use one gateway per independently controlled robot or joint group, and avoid overlapping actuator ranges.
- **Projects stay apart.** A Station never reaches a World in another project. Keep the World and the Robot Systems that drive it in the same project.

Step by step: [Drive Robots in the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md).

# Libraries

Libraries hold the files you reuse across Robot Systems and Robot Worlds: `.sdr` files, documents, scenes and other assets.

| Library             | Holds                                                   | Who sees it                         | Who adds and deletes files                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **My Library**      | Your personal files of any type                         | Only you                            | You                                                                                         |
| A project's library | Files shared with one project                           | Everyone with access to the project | The workspace's owner and admins, and members when **Members can manage the Library** is on |
| **Sodero Assets**   | Official robots, environments and documents from Sodero | Everyone                            | Nobody: it is read-only                                                                     |

The **Library** window lists the project libraries under **Workspace Library**, while some dialogs call the open project's library **Project Library**. Both names mean the project's library.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Open the Library

Click **Library** in the left navigation bar. The **Library** window has two tabs:

- **My Library**: your personal files.
- **Workspace Library**: the libraries of the workspace's projects. Click a project to see its files; the back arrow returns to the list of projects.

Both tabs have a search box, a type filter, a sort button and **Add file**. Each file has an **Export** button, which saves a copy on your computer, and a **Delete** button.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Add Files

1. In **My Library**, or in a project under **Workspace Library**, click **Add file**.
1. Choose the source:
   - **From your computer**: drag a file onto the dialog, or click **Choose file**.
   - In My Library, **Workspace Library**: copy a file from a project library you can open.
   - In a project's library, **My Library**: copy a file from your personal library.
1. Click **Add file**.

The library of Warehouse Demo under Workspace Library

A file can be up to 2 GiB.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Use Library Files

| File                                                                                        | Where you use it                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.sdr`                                                                                      | **Import** on the project page creates a Robot System or Robot World from it ([Import an .sdr File](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#2-import-an-sdr-file)) |
| Gateway and robot documents (`.gw`, `.sdd`, `.sddm`, `.sdda`), camera settings, map bundles | In the Station, when you load a document into a node ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md))                                |
| Scenes and assets (`.usd`, `.usda`, `.usdc`)                                                | In Studio, to build a World ([Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md))                                                                             |

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Delete Library Files

Click the file's **Delete** button. In a project's library, it is shown only to the people who may manage libraries.

**Deleting a library file removes it at once; it does not go to Trash.** Export a copy first if you may need the file again.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Sodero Assets

**Sodero Assets** is the official content that Sodero publishes for everyone: robots, grounds, lighting and sky images for Studio, and robot and gateway documents for **Manipulator**, **Mobile** and **Legged** robots in the Station.

Sodero Assets are read-only, and you can view, edit and simulate them only in Sodero. A World that uses them keeps them in Sodero: its local copy and its duplicates leave them out. An official Sodero World cannot be downloaded or duplicated.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Storage Limits

Your workspace's plan limits how much the libraries can hold. **Billing & Usage** shows the **Project libraries**, **Your My Library** and **Workspace storage** meters ([Credits and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/#limits)). A file that does not fit is refused with a message that names the limit: delete files you no longer need, or contact Sodero.

# Share and Collaborate

Work on a project with other people: invite them with a role, send them the project link and see who is working where. Sharing is set per project; membership of the workspace itself is covered in [Workspaces and People](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Invite People

Managers invite people from the project list:

1. Open the project's **⋯** menu and choose **Manage access**.
1. Under **Invite people**, type an email address, or pick one of the workspace members it suggests.
1. Choose the role: **Can manage**, **Can edit** (the default) or **Can view** ([Project Access and Roles](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#4-project-access-and-roles)).
1. Click **Invite**. The invitation goes out at once.

The Manage access dialog

The person receives an email titled *Sodero project access: Warehouse Demo* with a **Review access** button. The invitation is valid for 7 days; inviting the same address again replaces it. If the dialog says *Couldn't send invitation. Try again.*, check the address: the person may already have access.

### Change Roles, Remove People, Set the Access

**People with access** lists everyone in the project with their role.

- To change a role, use the person's role menu. To remove someone, click **X**.
- **Project access** at the top of the dialog switches between **Restricted** and **Workspace**.
- Click **Save** to apply these changes. **Cancel** drops them; invitations already sent stay.

You cannot change your own role, and a project always keeps at least one manager.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Accept an Invitation

The invited person clicks **Review access** in the email, signs in with the address the invitation was sent to and clicks **Accept invitation**. To decline, they ignore the email. Details and messages: [Accept an Invitation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/sign_in/#3-accept-an-invitation).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Guests

People invited to a project without being members of its workspace join it as **guests**. They find the project in the workspace menu under **Switch workspace › Guest projects (N)** ([Guest Projects](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/#guest-projects)). Inside the project, a guest has the role they were invited with, like anyone else.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Send the Project Link

Every project has a link that opens it in the portal. Copy it with **Manage access › Copy link**, with a file's **⋯ › Copy link**, with **AI agents › Copy project link**, or from the browser's address bar.

The link opens the project only for people who are signed in and have access to it, so invite new people first. The same applies to the link icon next to an active file's **Station · Live** or **Theater** link, which copies the address of that live view.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. See Who Is Working

The **Active users** column of the project page shows who is working in each file right now. Click the avatars for each person's name, role and activity:

| Activity                      | The person is                                            |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| *Station Design*              | Editing the Station in **Station · Edit**                |
| *Station open*                | Working in **Station · Live**                            |
| *Recent Station API activity* | Using the Station through an AI agent or the Project VPN |
| *Theater viewer*              | Watching the World in **Theater**                        |
| *Studio collaboration*        | Editing the World in **Studio**                          |

For recent activity in the whole workspace, such as projects created or files started and stopped, see [Notifications](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/#notifications).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Work Together on One Station or World

Several people can work in the same file at the same time:

- **Station.** Everyone who opens a Robot System works on the same Station.
- **Studio.** Everyone who opens a World in Studio joins the same editing session ([Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md)).
- **Theater.** Everyone who opens an active World watches the same simulation, each in their own [rendering mode](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#choose-rendering-mode). Each **RTX Real-time** viewer has its own cloud renderer, which uses credits.

People with **Can view** can look but not change anything. For example, **Go live** is disabled for them in **Station · Edit**.

**Tip:** Agree on who activates, runs, stops and deactivates a shared file. These actions change the file for everyone working in it.
# Build a World

# Studio

Studio is the World editor of Sodero Cloud. In it you build a Robot World: bring in a scene or Sodero Assets, arrange the objects, set mass and joint poses, and save. Its browser tab is titled *Cosmic Studio*.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Open Studio

1. On the project page, click **Studio** in the Robot World's **Actions** column. Studio opens only while the World is **Inactive** (or in **Error**): deactivate an active World first.
1. In **Choose rendering mode**, pick **RTX Real-time** or **WebGPU** and click **Open Cosmic Studio** ([Choose Rendering Mode](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#choose-rendering-mode)).
1. Studio opens in a new tab once its editing session has started.
1. The first time someone who can edit opens a new World, Studio adds a default environment from Sodero Assets: **Lighting** and **Ground**.
1. A World with several top-level USD files asks which one to open.
1. Keep the Sodero Cloud tab that opened Studio open while you work: Studio uses it to keep you signed in. If you close it, some actions say *Open Cosmic Studio from Sodero Cloud to use this.*

### The Studio Window

Studio with the warehouse World of the Quick Start

| Area             | What it holds                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Header**       | The project and World names, the renderer menu (**RTX Real-time** ▾), the session time, the save state (*Saved just now*), **Enter Theater** ▾, **Resources** ▾ and the people in the session |
| **Left rail**    | The Cosmic Studio menu (the logo), **Scene**, **Save now**, **Undo**, **Redo**, the asset libraries **Workspace** and **Sodero Assets**, and **Grid**                                         |
| **Scene** panel  | **Filter scene**, **+** to add a group or a light, and the **Hierarchy** of the World                                                                                                         |
| **Viewport**     | The World, with **Perspective** ▾ and **View** ▾ at the top left, the tools at the bottom, and the resolution and frame rate at the bottom right                                              |
| **Asset detail** | The properties of the selected object. The panel button at the top right of the viewport shows and hides it.                                                                                  |

The Cosmic Studio menu holds **Back to Sodero Cloud** (closes Studio), **Libraries**, **World**, **Edit**, **Help & Feedback** and **About Cosmic Studio**.

The World menu

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Bring Content In

### Replace the Whole Scene

Use it for a scene built elsewhere, for example in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

1. In the Cosmic Studio menu, choose **World › Replace scene…**.
1. On **This PC**, drag a USD file (`.usd`, `.usda`, `.usdc`) or a zipped USD folder (`.zip`) onto the dialog, or click **Choose file**. **My Library** and **Workspace Library** offer the USD files of your libraries.
1. Click **Replace** and confirm in the browser's dialog.
1. Studio says *Replaced with …*. If the **Hierarchy** still shows the old scene, reload the Studio page. Then click **Save now**.

The Replace scene dialog

- The unsaved edits of everyone in the session are discarded.
- A file can be up to 1 GiB. The scene must be Z-up: Studio refuses a Y-up scene ([Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md)).
- In a zip, keep the scene's main USD file at the top level, with the files it uses beside it or below it. Studio opens the USD file nearest to the top of the zip.

### Add Sodero Assets

1. Click **Sodero Assets** in the left rail. The **Asset Browser** opens.
1. Search by name, manufacturer, model or tags, filter with **All kinds**, **All categories** and **All manufacturers**, or browse the folders: environments, materials, objects, robots and scenes.
1. Select the asset and check **Parent prim** (where it goes, `/World` by default) and **Prim name** (its name in the World).
1. Click **Add Reference** (follows the source asset), **Add Payload** (a reference that loads on demand) or **Add Copy** (an independent copy).

The Asset Browser on the mobile robots of Sodero Assets

- For a material, select the object first, then open the browser and choose **Bind Material**.
- **Upload from PC** uploads a single USD file to the browser's **Workspace** library, from which you add it the same way. For a scene made of several files, use **Replace scene…** with a zip.
- Sodero Assets are official Sodero content: you can view, edit and simulate them in Sodero, but exports and downloads leave them out ([Libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/#5-sodero-assets)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Arrange and Edit

Select an object in the viewport or in the **Hierarchy**. The viewport outlines it, and **Asset detail** shows its properties.

The jackal selected in the Hierarchy and in the viewport

- **Move, rotate and scale.** Pick **Select**, **Move**, **Rotate** or **Scale** at the bottom of the viewport and drag the gizmo; **Snap** turns snapping on and off. Or type **Position**, **Rotation** (degrees) and **Scale** under **Transform**. A field applies when you press `Enter` or leave it.
- **Organize.** **+** in the Scene panel adds a **Group** or a light; a World without lights looks dark. Right-click a row for **Focus**, **Show** or **Hide**, **Lock** or **Unlock**, **Rename**, **Duplicate**, **Delete** and more. Drag a row onto another to move it under that object.
- **Physics.** Set the **Mass** (kg) or the **Density** (kg/m³) of the selected body.
- **Joints.** For a robot, **Joints** lists its movable joints in alphabetical order, for example **Joints (4)** for the Jackal. Pose a joint with **−** and **+** (5° or 5 cm per step) or type a value. **Reset pose** sets every joint back to zero.

Studio has no tools to create articulations, joints, colliders or cameras: prepare robots before you bring them in ([Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Save, Revisions and Export

| Action        | How                                                    | What happens                                                                                                                   |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Save**      | **Save now** in the left rail, or **World › Save now** | Writes the World to its files in the project. The header shows *Saved just now*.                                               |
| **Autosave**  | **World › Autosave** › 5, 10, 15 or 30 min             | Saves at that interval, every 10 minutes by default                                                                            |
| **Revisions** | **World › Show Revisions…**                            | **Create Revision** saves the World and keeps a copy. A revision's **⋯** menu offers **Restore this revision** and **Delete**. |
| **Export**    | **World › Export**                                     | Downloads the World: one `.usd` file, or a zip when the World uses other files                                                 |

- Activating a World loads its last saved state, so save before you activate. If the World is active while you save, the running World is updated.
- Restoring a revision first keeps the current state as a revision.
- An official Sodero World cannot be exported. When a World uses Sodero Assets, the export leaves those files out and says how many.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Work Together

- Everyone who opens the same World in Studio joins one editing session and sees the others' changes. The header shows who is there.
- Selecting an object reserves it for you: the others see who has it and cannot change it until you select something else.
- **Save now** and **Replace scene…** act on everyone's changes in the session.
- People with **Can view** see a **View only** badge. They can look around and inspect objects, but not change the World.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Keys and Camera

| Input                                   | Action                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Q`, `W`, `E`, `R`                      | **Select**, **Move**, **Rotate**, **Scale** tool                                               |
| `N`                                     | Snap on or off                                                                                 |
| `F`                                     | Frame the selection, or the whole World when nothing is selected                               |
| `Shift+F`, `Esc`                        | Follow the selection; stop following                                                           |
| Right-drag                              | Look around                                                                                    |
| Right-drag with `W` `A` `S` `D` `Q` `E` | Fly forward, left, back, right, down and up; `Shift` flies faster, the wheel changes the speed |
| Wheel, or `Alt` + right-drag            | Move closer or farther                                                                         |
| Middle-drag                             | Pan                                                                                            |
| `Alt` + left-drag                       | Orbit                                                                                          |

The keys are ignored while you type in a field.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Enter Theater

Click **Enter Theater** ▾ in the header and choose **RTX Real-time** or **WebGPU**. Studio activates the World if needed, which can take a minute, and opens it in [Theater](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/index.md) in a new tab. Once the World is active, the button reads **Open Theater**.

If another World of the project is active, Studio says **Another World is already running**: click **Open running World** to watch that one, or **Cancel**.

**An active World uses credits.** Enter Theater activates the World. Deactivate it on the project page when you are done ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md)).

# Prepare a World for Simulation

The Stations of a project can drive a robot in its Robot World only when the World follows a few rules. They are the rules for a robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim on Stellar X, plus two more: a purpose for robot cameras and a schema on fixed joints. The scene of the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md) follows all of them: use it as a model.

Studio has no tools to create articulations, joints, colliders or cameras. Prepare robots in a USD tool such as Isaac Sim ([Robot Setup](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/) in the Stellar X manual), then bring the scene into the World with **Replace scene…**. A robot in a single USD file can also come in through **Upload from PC** ([Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/#2-bring-content-in)).

______________________________________________________________________

## The Rules

| Rule                                                                                                              | Why                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **The World is Z-up, in meters, and has a PhysicsScene.**                                                         | Studio refuses Y-up scenes, and the simulation needs a physics scene.                               |
| **Each robot is one articulation.** Its top prim carries an **Articulation Root**.                                | A robot is simulated and driven as one articulation.                                                |
| **The prim name is the robot name.** It is unique in the World and equals the robot name in the gateway document. | A simulation gateway finds its robot by this name.                                                  |
| **Confirm the actuator mapping against the simulated joint order.**                                               | Each actuator index must address the intended movable joint.                                        |
| **Robot cameras have unique names and the purpose `guide`.**                                                      | A camera gateway reads its camera by name, and Sodero renders robot cameras that have this purpose. |
| **Fixed joints carry a physics joint schema.**                                                                    | A fixed joint without one takes no part in the simulation.                                          |

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Z-Up and a PhysicsScene

- Author the scene Z-up, in meters. Studio refuses a scene that declares Y-up: convert it before you bring it in.
- Include a **PhysicsScene** prim. Check that the **Hierarchy** in Studio shows one; the Quick Start's scene does.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. One Articulation per Robot

- The robot's top prim carries the **Articulation Root**. A robot has exactly one.
- Its links are rigid bodies with colliders and realistic masses. Studio can correct a body's mass or density ([Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/#3-arrange-and-edit)).
- The prim's name is the robot name: letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. It must be unique in the World, and case matters.
- The robot's simulation gateway uses the same name, from its gateway document (`.gw`). For the example scene, the Jackal articulation is `/World/jackal`.

**Names must match.** If the robot name in the gateway document differs from the robot's prim name, the robot never moves. Rename the prim, or use a gateway document with the right robot name.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Check the Actuator Mapping

Match each gateway actuator index to the intended movable joint in the simulation. Do not infer that mapping from an alphabetical list of joint names.

Select the robot in Studio and inspect **Joints (n)** to check its joint names and count. That list is alphabetical; it is not sufficient to establish the controller’s actuator order. Use robot documents prepared and validated for this scene and Station version ([Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md)).

Before normal operation, test one joint or wheel at a time with a small command and confirm that the intended part moves in the intended direction. Stop and correct the actuator mapping or axis configuration if it does not. Keep joint limits consistent with the robot model.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Cameras and IMUs

**Cameras.** A camera gateway reads one camera of the World by its name.

- Put each robot camera, a **Camera** prim, under the link it is mounted on, so that it moves with the robot.
- Give it a unique name. The camera gateway's camera name is this prim name: letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`.
- Set the camera's **purpose** to `guide`. Robot cameras need this purpose in Sodero Cloud; a camera without it is not rendered for the Station.

While the World is active, Sodero renders its robot cameras for the camera gateways of the project's Stations. Theater's loading screen shows their progress under **Robot cameras**.

**IMUs.** An IMU gateway reads an IMU on a link of the robot. Declare it on the robot prim with `rc:imuLink`, the name of the link, and `rc:imuOffset`, its position on that link in meters, as for Isaac Sim ([Robot Setup › IMU](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/#7-imu)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Fixed Joints

A fixed joint holds a body in place, for example the base of a manipulator on the world. Give every fixed joint a physics joint schema, such as `PhysxJointAPI`. Without one, the joint takes no part in the simulation in Sodero Cloud, and a fixed-base robot falls over.

In Isaac Sim, you can set a camera's purpose and a fixed joint's schema with **Window › Script Editor**, then save the scene:

```
import omni.usd
from pxr import PhysxSchema, UsdGeom

stage = omni.usd.get_context().get_stage()

# a robot camera: purpose guide
camera = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/my_robot/links/base_link/cam0")
UsdGeom.Imageable(camera).CreatePurposeAttr().Set(UsdGeom.Tokens.guide)

# the fixed joint that holds my_arm to the world: a physics joint schema
anchor = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/my_arm/joints/anchor")
PhysxSchema.PhysxJointAPI.Apply(anchor)
```

Replace the prim paths with those of your scene.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Keep the World Light

- Everything in the World is drawn, but only physics content takes part in the simulation: the physics scene, rigid bodies, colliders, joints and articulations. Give physics only to what the robots touch.
- Large scenes take longer to load. Theater reports a World that has not loaded within 3 minutes. A file you bring into Studio can be up to 1 GiB.
- Watch **Physics RTF** in Theater. Near 1.00, the simulation keeps up with real time; if it stays well below 1.00, make the World lighter.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Test the World in Theater

Check the World on its own before you connect Stations to it:

1. Save the World in Studio and close Studio.
1. On the project page, activate the World.
1. Open **Theater** and wait until the World, and its **Robot cameras** if it has any, have loaded.
1. Click **Start Theater**.
1. Check that:
   - the robots rest on the ground and do not fall through it or drift away;
   - a fixed-base robot stays in place;
   - **Physics RTF** is near 1.00;
   - each robot appears in **Scene assets** under the name its gateway document uses.
1. Click **Stop Theater**. To change the World, deactivate it and open it in Studio.

Next: [Drive Robots in the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md).
# Configure a Robot System

# Stellar Station

Every Robot System is one **Stellar Station** ("the Station"). In the Station you build the robot system as a graph of nodes, give the nodes their documents, start them, and watch their state and logs. This manual describes the Station opened from the Sodero Cloud portal; device versions may differ.

______________________________________________________________________

## What a Robot System Is

A Robot System holds one Station and everything it needs:

| Part                   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node graph             | Gateways, controllers, compounds and applications, and the connections between their ports ([Build the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/index.md)) |
| Documents and settings | Gateway and robot documents, camera files, map bundles and node settings ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md))        |
| Apps and modules       | The Store apps and your own module packages that the nodes run ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md))                            |

A Robot System drives robots in the project's active Robot World ([Drive Robots in the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md)). You create it on the project page ([Robot Systems and Robot Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/index.md)). Nodes, ports and node types are explained in [Key Concepts](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Open the Station

On the project page, the Robot System's **Actions** column holds the link:

- **Station · Edit** while the Robot System is inactive. It opens the Edit page.
- **Station · Live** while it is active. It opens the Live page; opening it does not start any node.

The Station opens in a new browser tab and uses your portal sign-in. The header shows the project and the Robot System, for example *Warehouse Demo / jackal*. People with **Can view** can open both pages, but every control that changes something is disabled for them ([Project Access and Roles](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#4-project-access-and-roles)).

### Edit and Live

The Station has two pages for the same Robot System:

|                 | Edit page                                                                | Live page                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Badge           | **EDIT**                                                                 | **LIVE**, with how long the Station has been live                                                                                     |
| The Station     | Inactive: nothing runs and no credits are used                           | Active: it uses credits ([Credits and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md))                    |
| What you can do | Add, connect, rename and delete nodes; set parameters; select Store apps | Upload and confirm controller documents while their nodes are stopped, then start nodes, inspect logs and open available operator UIs |
| Button          | **Go live**                                                              | **Stop live**                                                                                                                         |

The Edit page of a new Robot System

- **Go live** activates the Station, like **Active** in the portal's **Activation** column. A banner follows the start, and **Cancel** stops it. When the Station is ready, usually after about a minute, the tab moves on to the Live page by itself.
- **Stop live** asks first: *Every node stops and the system goes back to edit mode. Nodes and connections stay saved.* It deactivates the Station, like **Deactivate** in the portal, and the tab returns to the Edit page.
- When someone else activates the Station while you are on the Edit page, your tab moves on to the Live page as well.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Screen Layout

| Area      | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Header    | Project and Robot System, the **EDIT** or **LIVE** badge, **Go live** or **Stop live**, **Resources**, and the people who have the Station open                                                                                                                   |
| Left rail | **Runtime** (the graph), **Modules** and **Store** ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)); at the bottom **Notifications**, **Help** and your account                                                            |
| Toolbar   | The save state (**Saved**), **Filter**, **Load YAML**, **Export** and **Add node**. The Live page adds **Package** and **Start all nodes**, and **Adopt running** when something runs that the graph does not show. The last button shows or hides the inspector. |
| Canvas    | The node cards and their connections. At the bottom: zoom, **Fit view**, **Auto layout**, and folding or unfolding all cards.                                                                                                                                     |
| Inspector | The selected node: name, module and state, **Connection**, **Parameters** and settings, **Logs** (Live page only) and **Activity**                                                                                                                                |

The Sodero mark at the top left opens the Station menu: **Back to Sodero Cloud**, **Libraries** (**My Library**, **Project Library**), **Theme** (**Midnight** or **Twilight**), **Help & Feedback** and **About Stellar Station**.

**Tip:** Right-click the empty canvas to add a node, and right-click a node for its actions.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. What Is Saved Where

| What                        | Where it is kept                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Changes to the graph        | Saved automatically on both pages. The toolbar shows **Saving…**, then **Saved**; if a save fails, it shows **Retry save**. Changes made on the Live page stay after **Stop live**.                                                                       |
| Documents and settings      | With the Robot System. The Station saves them when it is deactivated and restores them when it is activated. Upload robot documents from the Live page ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)). |
| Store apps and your modules | Recorded with the Robot System and installed each time the Station starts ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md))                                                                                         |
| The whole Robot System      | **Download local copy** on the project page saves it as an `.sdr` file ([Download a Local Copy](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#6-download-a-local-copy))                                                                   |

**Export** in the toolbar saves the graph only, not the documents or apps ([Load and Export the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#6-load-and-export-the-graph)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Resources

Click **Resources** in the header to see the Station's **CPU**, **RAM** and **GPU** load. The bars turn amber at 70 % and red at 85 %. **—** means that no value is reported; on the Edit page every value is **—** (*Usage appears once the system is live.*). **View details** opens the system monitor.

Sodero Cloud gives each Station its own share of CPU and memory. The project page also shows the Station's use in its **Resource** column; hover over it for the Station's CPUs and its memory limit ([The Project Page](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#3-the-project-page)). When a Station runs close to its limits, give it fewer nodes, for example by putting each robot in its own Robot System.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. What You Do on the Station

```
flowchart LR
 A["Select apps"] --> B["Add and connect nodes"]
 B --> C["Go live"]
 C --> D["Upload and confirm documents"]
 D --> E["Run World and start nodes"]
 E --> F["Open available operator UI"]
```

| Step                                        | Page                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Install the apps that your nodes run        | [Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Add nodes and connect their ports           | [Build the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Give the nodes their documents and settings | [Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Start nodes, read their state and logs      | [Run and Monitor](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Connect the robots to the World             | [Drive Robots in the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md)                                                                                                                                                            |
| Drive and teach the robots                  | [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md), [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md), [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/articulation/index.md) |

For a first walkthrough with a simulated robot, follow the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md).

# Apps and Packages

Check the app itself in **Store**. A **Starting apps** bundle is a selection of apps, not confirmation that every required app is installed or available for the current environment. Verify the gateway and controller separately after going live.

Every node of a Station runs an app or module that is installed on that Station. **Add node** offers only what is installed, plus empty drafts. Apps come from the **Store**; your own programs are uploaded as module packages. Both are kept with the Robot System and installed each time its Station starts.

| Source          | What it is                                                                        | Badge in **Add node** | Where you install it                                             |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Store app       | A program published by Sodero, such as the actuator gateway or a robot controller | **SODERO**            | **Store** in the left rail                                       |
| Your own module | A module package (`.tar.gz`) that you built                                       | **CUSTOM**            | **Modules › Add custom module**, or **Package** on the Live page |

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Starting Apps

When you create a Robot System, **Starting apps** offers bundles of Store apps, for example for a manipulator or a mobile robot. **Empty** has none ([Create a File](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#1-create-a-file)). The apps of the chosen bundle are recorded with the Robot System and install when the Station first starts.

If **Add node** lists only **Empty gateway**, **Empty controller** and the other drafts, no app is installed yet. Install the apps you need from the Store.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. The Store

Click **Store** in the left rail. The Store lists the apps that Sodero publishes, one row each.

The Store of a new Robot System, on the Edit page

| Part of a row | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Name          | The app and a short description, for example **Gateway Designer** (*Gateway control and setup workspace*)                                                                                                                                  |
| **Included**  | Every Store app is included in Sodero Cloud; there is nothing to buy                                                                                                                                                                       |
| State         | **Not Installed** or **Installed**                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Versions      | *Current* (the Store's release), *Installed version*, *New* when a newer release is out, and *Installed* (the date). An installed app also lists its *Cloud permissions*: what its own UI may use in Sodero Cloud, such as your libraries. |
| Buttons       | **Install** or **Uninstall**, and **Update** when a newer release is out                                                                                                                                                                   |

### Install

Click **Install**. When the app installs depends on the page:

- **Edit page:** the app is recorded for the Robot System and installs when the Station starts.
- **Live page:** the app installs at once and is recorded for the Station's later starts.

The app then appears in **Add node**, under the node type it declares, with the **SODERO** badge ([Add a Node](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#1-add-a-node)).

### Update

**Update** (*Update to …*) replaces the installed release with the Store's current one. While a node of the app runs, the button is disabled (*Stop its running instances to update it*): stop those nodes first. On the Edit page, **Update** records the new release, which installs when the Station starts.

### Uninstall

**Uninstall** removes the app from the Robot System. While a node of the app runs, the button is disabled. While the saved graph still has nodes of the app, it is refused with a message that names them: delete those nodes, then uninstall.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Your Own Modules

### The Modules Page

Click **Modules** in the left rail. *Used modules in this system* lists the Station's modules with **Name**, **Type**, **Publisher** (**Sodero** or **Custom**), **Version** and **Used by**, the number of nodes that use each one. The **⋯** menu of a row offers **Module info** (version, publisher, source, size and the nodes that use it) and **Remove module**.

### Upload a Module Package

1. Click **Add custom module**.
1. Drop one or more packages (`.tar.gz` or `.tgz`) on the dialog, or click to choose them.
1. Click **Add module** (**Add N modules** for several).

On the Live page, **Package** in the toolbar does the same from the graph: choose one or more packages, and they upload one after another (*Uploading 1/2 · …*).

As with Store apps, a package uploaded on the Edit page installs when the Station starts, and one uploaded on the Live page installs at once. Either way it is kept with the Robot System. Your module then appears in **Add node** under the type it declares, with the **CUSTOM** badge.

How to build a module package is described in [Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/extend/custom_modules/) in the Stellar X manual. In Sodero Cloud:

- **Stations run on x86-64 computers.** Build the native programs in your package for x86-64 (`amd64`).
- **Keep packages small.** Every uploaded package is installed again each time the Station starts, so large packages make starting and stopping slower.

### Remove a Module

Stop and delete the nodes that use the module, then choose **⋯ › Remove module** in its row. The dialog says how many nodes still use it; click **Remove** to confirm.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Messages

| Message                                                                                       | What to do                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *… is not a package archive (a .tar.gz) …* or *… the file name must end with .tar.gz or .tgz* | Choose the package archive itself: a gzip-compressed `.tar.gz` or `.tgz` file                                                                             |
| *… the limit for a package archive (.tar.gz) is 360 MB.*                                      | Make the package smaller                                                                                                                                  |
| *… is built into this Station and cannot be replaced by an upload.*                           | The Station has its own version of this package. Leave it out of the upload.                                                                              |
| *Package is running; stop its active instances before removing it: …*                         | Stop the listed nodes, then try again                                                                                                                     |
| *This package is used by the saved graph. Remove these nodes first: …*                        | Delete the listed nodes, then try again                                                                                                                   |
| *Install the package of … (…) from the Store first. Nothing was started.*                     | A node's app is not installed on this Station. Install it, then start the nodes again.                                                                    |
| *It is installed now but may be gone after this Station stops and starts again: …*            | The app runs now, but Sodero Cloud could not record it for the Robot System. After the next start, check the Store and install it again if it is missing. |
| *It is removed now but may come back after this Station stops and starts again: …*            | After the next start, check the Store and uninstall it again if it is back                                                                                |
| *Install failed*, *Update failed* or *Uninstall failed*                                       | Try again. If it fails again, reload the page.                                                                                                            |
| **Package error** with *Could not load the Store.* or *Could not load the item's packages.*   | The Edit page could not read the apps. Reload the page.                                                                                                   |

# Build the Graph

A Station is a graph of **nodes** connected through **ports**. This page shows how to add and name nodes, connect them, and keep a large graph tidy. You can change the graph on the Edit page and on the Live page; every change is saved automatically. The node types are explained in [Key Concepts](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Add a Node

1. Click **Add node** in the toolbar, or right-click the empty canvas.

1. Choose the node type: **Gateway**, **Controller**, **Compound** or **Application**.

   Choosing the node type

1. Under **Select a module**, choose the app or module, then click **Next**.

   Gateway › sodero.actuator_gateway

1. Enter the node name and click **Add node**. You can rename the node later.

   Naming the node

The node appears on the canvas as **Planned**. Nothing runs until you start it on the Live page ([Run and Monitor](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)).

### The Module List

| Badge      | Entry                                                                              | Detail line                                                                                                                             |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **SODERO** | An app installed from the Store                                                    | *Sodero package ·* and its version                                                                                                      |
| **CUSTOM** | A module package you uploaded                                                      | *Imported package · Installed*                                                                                                          |
| **DRAFT**  | **Empty gateway**, **Empty controller**, **Empty compound**, **Empty application** | *Empty subsystem to develop yourself (no package)*: a placeholder with no program behind it, for sketching a system. It does not start. |

Each type lists only the apps and modules installed on this Station. To add another, install it first ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).

### Name the Node

The name field proposes the app's own name, for example `sodero.actuator_gateway`. Add a last part that names the robot or device, so that the name reads `sodero.<package>.<name>`:

| Node                                     | Example name                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Actuator gateway of a robot              | `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal` |
| Mobile base controller of the same robot | `sodero.mlc.jackal`              |
| Manipulator controller                   | `sodero.mmc.arm`                 |
| Articulation controller                  | `sodero.amc.dog`                 |
| Strider                                  | `sodero.strider`                 |

- **The last part names the node's documents.** A new document you upload to `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal` is named `jackal` ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
- **Robot documents refer to their gateway by its node name**, for example `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal`. Give the gateway the name its controller's document expects.
- **Give a robot's gateway and controller the same last part.** The graph stays easy to read.
- Names use letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, start with a letter or digit, and have up to 60 characters (an empty draft: 20). Each name can be used once per Station: *… is already a node of this graph: use another id, e.g. ….2.*

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Node Cards

| Part             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Title            | The node name                                                                                                                                          |
| Second line      | The app or module the node runs                                                                                                                        |
| **REQUIRES n/m** | Ports the node needs from other nodes, on the left edge of the card: connected / total                                                                 |
| **PROVIDES n/m** | Ports the node offers, on the right edge: ports with at least one connection / total                                                                   |
| State            | **Planned** until the node first starts, then its running state ([Node States](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#4-node-states)) |

The card border has the color of the node type: orange for gateways, blue-violet for controllers, purple for compounds and mint for applications. The arrow at the top right of a card folds its ports away.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Connect Ports

Connect a port that one node requires to a matching port that another node provides:

- **Drag** from one port dot to the other.
- **Click** one port, then the other.
- In the inspector of the node that requires the port, click **Auto-connect** next to the port. The Station connects the first matching port it finds, or shows *No match*.

The Station accepts a connection only when the two ports are on different nodes, one requires and the other provides, and both use the same interface. The inspector shows each port's interface under its name, for example `api.actuator.servo.v1`. The Station also keeps the system's structure:

- Only a controller may use a gateway.
- An application uses controllers or compounds, never gateways directly.
- One controller drives a gateway.

A refused connection says why, for example *Connect ports on different nodes with opposite directions and matching contracts.*

To remove a connection, select the node and click **Disconnect** next to the port in the inspector.

**Check Auto-connect with several robots.** Auto-connect does not look at node names: with two gateways in the graph, it may pick the other robot's. Check the result, or drag the connection yourself.

### Common Connections

| Node (requires)                                               | Port           | Connect to (provides)                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sodero.mmc.<name>`, `sodero.mlc.<name>`, `sodero.amc.<name>` | `servo_link`   | The robot's actuator gateway `sodero.actuator_gateway.<name>`, port `servo_link` |
| `sodero.strider`                                              | `mobile_base`  | The mobile base controller `sodero.mlc.<name>`, port `mobile_base`               |
| `sodero.strider`                                              | `localization` | The localizer, `sodero.localizer`                                                |
| `sodero.strider`                                              | `navigation`   | The navigator, `sodero.navigator`                                                |

Strider drives what its ports are connected to ([Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Rename and Delete

- **Rename:** click the pencil next to the node name in the inspector and enter the new name. The node keeps its connections and the documents it uses.
- **Delete:** right-click the node and choose **Delete node**. The dialog asks *Delete "…" from this robot system?*; click **Delete node**. The node's connections are removed too.

On the Live page, stop a node before you rename or delete it.

Deleting a node cannot be undone. Everyone working on the Station sees the change at once.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Find Your Way in a Large Graph

- **Filter** shows only nodes of one **Node type** or **Status**; **Reset all** clears it.
- **Fit view** zooms to show every node; **Auto layout** arranges the nodes by their connections.
- The **N issues** chip at the left of the toolbar lists problems, such as *Required port "servo_link" is not connected*. **Locate** jumps to the node.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Load and Export the Graph

- **Export** downloads the graph as a `.yaml` file. If something runs on the Live page that the graph does not show, it asks first: **Planned topology only** or **Also include what is running**.
- **Load YAML** loads such a file from your PC, **My Library** or the **Project Library**. It replaces the nodes and connections of the Station (*… loaded — N nodes now in the system.*).

The file holds the graph only: nodes, their parameters and their connections. Documents, settings and apps are not part of it. To copy a whole Robot System, use **Duplicate file**, or **Download local copy** and **Import**, on the project page ([Robot Systems and Robot Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/index.md)).

# Documents and Settings

Most nodes work from a **document**: a gateway runs a gateway document (`.gw`), a robot controller runs a robot document (`.sdd`, `.sddm` or `.sdda`). Some apps also have **settings** that you edit in the node's inspector. This page shows how to give a node its document, which kinds exist, and how to change settings.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Choose or Upload a Document

Select the node. The **Parameters** section of its inspector has one field for each document the app reads, for example **Gateway project** on an actuator gateway or **document (robot)** on a controller.

The inspector of a new actuator gateway: no document yet

- The dropdown lists existing documents and may offer **Built-in default (no document)**. For robot operation, select the document intended for that robot; do not treat an empty document field as proof that its controller is configured.
- The line under it tells where the document came from, for example *Uploaded: jackal.gw · 1 KB · …*, or *Not uploaded*.
- **Upload** brings in a new document.

### Upload a Document

1. Click **Upload** under the field. The dialog is named after the kind, for example **Upload gateway-project document** or **Upload robot document**.

1. Choose where the file comes from:

   | Tab                   | Files                                                                                                        |
   | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
   | **From your PC**      | Drop the file on the dialog, or click **Choose file**                                                        |
   | **My Library**        | Your personal library                                                                                        |
   | **Workspace Library** | This project's library ([Libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/index.md)) |
   | **Sodero Assets**     | Robot and gateway documents published by Sodero, under **Manipulator**, **Mobile** and **Legged**            |

1. Click **Import**.

Uploading a gateway document from your PC

The same dialog for a robot document

The Station confirms the upload, for example *jackal.gw uploaded as the gateway-project document jackal*, and the node takes the new document. If the upload fails, the message says why: *… was not uploaded — …*.

- A new document is named after the last part of the node name: for `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal` it is `jackal` ([Name the Node](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#name-the-node)).
- If the field already names a document, the upload replaces that document.

**Upload robot documents from the Live page.** Go live first, then upload `.sdd`, `.sddm` and `.sdda` documents in the controller's inspector.

After the upload, reopen the node and confirm that the intended document is still selected. Upload controller documents on the Live page, while the node is stopped, before starting it.

### Rules

- **A running node keeps its document.** Stop the node before you upload a new document for it or change its settings.
- **Each controller takes its own kind:** `.sdd` for `sodero.mmc`, `.sddm` for `sodero.mlc`, `.sdda` for `sodero.amc`.
- **A robot document names its gateway** and the gateway's actuators it uses. Connect the controller's `servo_link` to that gateway, and give the gateway at least as many actuators as the document uses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Kinds of Documents

| Kind             | File                                                                                      | Used by                                                       |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gateway document | `.gw`                                                                                     | Actuator gateways, `sodero.actuator_gateway.<name>`           |
| Robot document   | `.sdd` (manipulator), `.sddm` (mobile base), `.sdda` (articulated robot)                  | `sodero.mmc.<name>`, `sodero.mlc.<name>`, `sodero.amc.<name>` |
| Camera document  | `.yaml`                                                                                   | Camera gateways, `sodero.camera_gateway.<name>`               |
| Map bundle       | A `.nav` folder packed as `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tar` or `.zip`, for example `site.nav.tgz` | The localizer, the navigator and visual odometry              |

A Station has **one map bundle**: the localizer, the navigator and visual odometry share it, and a new upload replaces it. What a map bundle holds is described in [Load and Configure a Map](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/navigation/map_bundle/) in the Stellar X manual.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Settings

Some apps declare settings. The inspector then shows one section per settings file below **Parameters**, titled by the app.

1. Stop the node if it runs.
1. Change the fields.
1. Click **Save settings** (*Settings saved.*). **Reload** discards your changes.
1. When the settings belong to a document, the section shows once the node has one: *Choose or upload a … document in Parameters; its … settings then appear here.*
1. Some apps can create the file for you: click **Create with defaults**.
1. The fields themselves come from each app.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Make Documents in Stellar Designer

Gateway and robot documents are made in **Stellar Designer**: the Gateway Designer makes `.gw` documents, and the manipulator, mobile robot and articulation editors make `.sdd`, `.sddm` and `.sdda` documents. Every editor and field is described in the Stellar X manual: [Stellar Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/tutorials/stellar_designer/introduction/) and [Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/gateways/gateway_designer/).

- A simulation gateway's document also names the robot it drives in the World ([Drive Robots in the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md)).
- Ready-made documents for Sodero's robots are in **Sodero Assets**.

### Documents with Old Node Names

Documents made before the node names changed to `sodero.…` still name nodes `rc.…`, for example `rc.actuator_gateway.jackal`. The Station refuses them: the message says that the file *uses an obsolete format*, or names an *Obsolete robot file* or an *Obsolete gateway filename*. Export the document again from a current Stellar Designer and upload the new file.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Messages

| Message                                                                                                                        | What to do                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *Only … files can be imported.*                                                                                                | The file has the wrong extension for this field. Check the kind in the dialog's title.                     |
| *… is not a robot document (expected a .sdd, .sddm or .sdda file).*                                                            | Export the robot from Stellar Designer as `.sdd` (manipulator), `.sddm` (mobile) or `.sdda` (articulation) |
| *… uses an obsolete format. …*                                                                                                 | The document still uses old node names ([Documents with Old Node Names](#documents-with-old-node-names))   |
| *Robot '…' cannot take a new file while …*, *Gateway '…' is in use: …* or *Stop the camera before replacing its configuration* | A running node uses the document. Stop the node, then upload again.                                        |
| *Stop this node before changing its settings: …*                                                                               | Stop the node, then save the settings again                                                                |
| *… is an archive but not a .nav bundle (no localizer.yaml inside).* or *…: the .nav bundle is incomplete — missing …*          | Pack the localizer's `.nav` folder itself as `.tar.gz` or `.zip`, and upload that                          |
| *… is yaml but not a camera_gateway config …*                                                                                  | The file is not a camera document                                                                          |
| *Another editor changed this robot file first — reload …*                                                                      | Someone else changed the document at the same time. Reload, then repeat your change.                       |

# Drive Robots in the World

The Robot Systems of a project drive the robots in the project's active Robot World. Sodero Cloud makes the connection: a simulation gateway reaches the World by itself and finds its robot by name. This page shows what to set so that a robot moves.

```
flowchart LR
    subgraph RS ["Robot System"]
        C["Controller<br>sodero.mlc.jackal"] -- servo_link --> G["Simulation gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal<br>robot name: jackal"]
    end
    subgraph W ["Robot World, active"]
        R["Robot prim jackal<br>joints 1 to 4"]
    end
    G -- "found by name" --> R
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. What Is Automatic

- **No address to set.** The simulation, camera and IMU gateways of an active Station connect to the project's active World by themselves. A simulator address stored in a gateway document is ignored.
- **Activate in any order.** A Station that is active before the World connects once the World is up.
- **One World per project.** Only one Robot World of a project can be active at a time, and a Station never reaches a World in another project ([How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#4-how-robot-worlds-and-robot-systems-work-together)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Name the Robot

Use a simulation gateway document configured for the robot in the World. Its robot name must match the articulation prim name. Depending on the document and app release, the name can be supplied in the document or in the supported node settings. Check the applied name before starting; do not assume renaming a node changes its simulation target.

**The robot name must be exactly the name of the robot's articulation prim in the World.**

| Station                                                   | World                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gateway document `jackal.gw` with the robot name `jackal` | The robot's articulation prim `jackal`, at `/World/jackal` in the World's hierarchy |

- Names are case-sensitive: `Jackal` and `jackal` are different robots.
- A robot name uses letters, digits and `_`, and does not start with a digit.
- Every robot in the World needs a name of its own.

If the names differ, the gateway never finds its robot: it keeps waiting, and the robot does not move.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Match Actuators and Joints

The gateway addresses joints by actuator index. Confirm the simulator's joint order and use the matching robot document; an alphabetical joint list in Studio does not establish that order.

| Gateway                               | Robot in the World                      |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Actuators 1, 2, 3, 4 (indices 0 to 3) | The robot's 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th joint |

- Give the gateway one actuator per joint it drives. The robot document then maps the gateway's actuators to its joints or wheels ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
- To drive one robot with two gateways, for example an arm and its gripper, set the gripper gateway's **DOF offset** to the index of the gripper's first joint ([Gateway Designer › Simulation Gateways](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/gateways/gateway_designer/#5-simulation-gateways) in the Stellar X manual).

What a robot needs in the World, such as its articulation and joint drives, is described in [Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Several Robots and Stations

- Use one gateway and one controller per robot, each gateway with its own robot name.
- The gateways can sit in one Robot System or in several. Every active Robot System of the project connects to the same World.
- Drive each robot, or each part of a robot, from one gateway only.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Cameras and IMUs

- **Camera gateway** (`sodero.camera_gateway.<name>`): its camera name must be the name of the camera's prim in the World. It uses letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`. The World renders the robots' cameras while it is active; the first pictures can take a moment after the World starts.
- **IMU gateway** (`sodero.imu_gateway.<name>`): it reads the IMU of one robot, which you name like the robot of an actuator gateway.

The World must declare its cameras and IMUs ([Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Start Order

1. **Activate** the Robot World and the Robot System on the project page. **Go live** in the Station also activates the Robot System.
1. **Run** the World on the project page, so that it plays ([Run and Stop](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#2-run-and-stop)).
1. **Start the nodes**: **Start all nodes** on the Live page, or **Run** the Robot System on the project page. Selecting the World and the Robot System together and choosing **Actions › Run** plays the World and starts the nodes in one step ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#how-it-works)).
1. Open the controller UI and switch the servo on ([Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md), [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md), [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/articulation/index.md)).

Stopping the World resets its robots' poses. After you run it again, check the controllers: if their servos are off, switch them on again.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Troubleshooting

A gateway connects to the World, not to another node. A World that is not running, or a robot name that does not match, therefore shows neither as **Waiting binding** nor as an error in the graph: the gateway's node can look normal while the gateway waits for its robot. Select the gateway and read its **Gateway events** log ([Logs and Activity](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#5-logs-and-activity)). It says whether the gateway is still waiting for its robot or is connected to the simulation.
