| Symptom                                                        | What to check                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The gateway keeps waiting for its robot                        | The World is active and playing; it is in the same project; the robot name equals the robot's prim name exactly                                                        |
| The controller stays in **Waiting binding**                    | Its `servo_link` is connected to the gateway, and the gateway runs ([Node States](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#4-node-states))              |
| The servo switches on, but the robot does not move             | The gateway has as many actuators as the robot document uses. In Strider, the drive mode is **Twist**.                                                                 |
| A wheel or joint turns the wrong way, or the wrong joint moves | Stop motion and check joint order, actuator mapping, axis direction and configured polarity. Change the appropriate document setting, then verify one joint at a time. |
| The servo switched off by itself                               | The World may have been stopped or reset. Switch the servo on again.                                                                                                   |
| The camera gateway shows no picture                            | The camera name equals the camera's prim name; the World plays and declares its cameras                                                                                |
| The robot moves slower than expected                           | In Theater, **Physics RTF** is below 1.00: the World simulates slower than real time ([Theater](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/index.md))   |
# Run and Monitor

# Activate and Run

Each Robot System and Robot World has its own cloud environment. **Activate** prepares it, **Run** starts its work, **Stop** ends the work, and **Deactivate** releases the environment. Stopping a World resets its pose and clock; it is not a pause that preserves progress.

**An active environment uses credits.** It is billed for every minute it is active, whether or not anybody uses it or anything runs in it. Stop does not end that; Deactivate does ([Credits and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## How It Works

Two columns of the project page control a file: **Activation** brings its environment up or down, and **Running** starts or stops what runs in it.

```
flowchart LR
    I["Inactive"] -- "Activate" --> S["Active<br>Stopped"]
    S -- "Run" --> R["Active<br>Running"]
    R -- "Stop" --> S
    S -- "Deactivate" --> I
    R -- "Deactivate" --> I
```

| Action         | Robot System                                                                           | Robot World                                                                           | Credits     |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| **Activate**   | Starts the environment and restores the Station's saved data and apps. No node starts. | Starts the environment and loads the World's scene. The simulation does not play yet. | Use begins  |
| **Run**        | Starts every saved node, like **Start all nodes** on Stellar X                         | Plays the simulation                                                                  | No change   |
| **Stop**       | Stops the nodes                                                                        | Stops the simulation and resets the World's pose and clock                            | Use goes on |
| **Deactivate** | Stops the nodes, saves the Station's data, then tears the environment down             | Tears the environment down                                                            | Use ends    |

A typical session: select the Robot World and the Robot Systems that drive it, choose **Actions › Activate**, then **Actions › Run**. Watch the World in **Theater** and work with the robots in **Station · Live**. **Stop** when you pause, and **Deactivate** when you are done.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Activate and Deactivate

Click the state in a file's **Activation** column and choose **Active** to activate the file, or **Inactive** to deactivate it.

The Activation menu of the Robot System jackal

While the file activates, it shows **Activating** and the current step, for example *Station starting* or *World starting*. It is usually **Active** after about a minute.

jackal activating: Station starting

| State            | Meaning                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Inactive**     | Not active. Uses no credits.                                                                  |
| **Activating**   | Coming up. You can already choose **Inactive**.                                               |
| **Active**       | Up, and using credits                                                                         |
| **Deactivating** | Going down. This cannot be interrupted.                                                       |
| **Error**        | The activation failed, or the environment stopped unexpectedly. Open the menu for the reason. |

- After an **Error**, choose **Active** to try again, or select the file and choose **Actions › Deactivate** to release it.
- Only one Robot World per project can be active ([How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#4-how-robot-worlds-and-robot-systems-work-together)).

A chip next to the column shows each result, for example *Environment active* or *Failed*. Click *Failed* to read the message.

While a request runs, the menu also offers **Cancel workflow (no rollback)**. It stops the request but undoes nothing: an environment that already came up stays active, and keeps using credits, until you deactivate it.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Run and Stop

Once a file is **Active**, click the state in its **Running** column and choose **Running** or **Stopped**.

A World without a scene cannot run: build it in [Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md) first. **Stopped** keeps the file active, so it keeps using credits.

| State              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Running**        | Operations are running                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Partly running** | Robot System only: some nodes did not start. A **Failed** badge and a banner above the tables explain why. Open **Station · Live** and read that node's log ([Run and Monitor](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)). |
| **Stopped**        | Operations are stopped. Also shown while the file is not active.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Error**          | The World reported an error                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **-**              | The state cannot be read. People with **Can view** always see **-**.                                                                                                                                                                              |

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Open a File

The **Actions** column holds the links that open a file in a new browser tab. A dimmed link tells you on hover why it cannot open now.

| Link               | Opens when                                      | Opens                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Station · Edit** | The Robot System is not active                  | The Station editor. Its **Go live** button activates the Station.                                             |
| **Station · Live** | The Robot System is **Active**                  | The running Station ([Stellar Station](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/overview/index.md)) |
| **Studio**         | The Robot World is **Inactive** or in **Error** | The World editor ([Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md))                |
| **Theater**        | The Robot World is **Active**                   | The live view of the World ([Theater](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/index.md))    |

Opening a file never starts nodes or plays a World. To edit an active World in Studio, deactivate it first.

### Choose Rendering Mode

Before Studio or Theater opens, the portal asks how to draw the World on your screen.

| Mode              | Draws the World                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **RTX Real-time** | On a cloud GPU, with advanced materials and lighting. Each Studio or Theater tab in this mode runs its own cloud renderer, which uses credits. |
| **WebGPU**        | In your browser, on this device's GPU. Performance depends on your hardware.                                                                   |

Pick a mode and click **Open Cosmic Studio** or **Open Cosmic Theater**. **Remember on this device.** preselects your choice next time. The mode only changes how you see the World, not the simulation, and each person chooses their own.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Several Files at Once

Editors and managers can handle several files together from the selection bar.

1. Select the files: click their rows, or tick the box at the end of a row. A selection holds any number of Robot Systems and at most one Robot World.
1. Open **Actions** and choose an item.
1. Follow the progress in the files' chips and in the log under the selection bar.

jackal and warehouse selected, with the Actions menu open

The menu offers **Activate**, **Run**, **Stop** and **Deactivate**, which act on every selected file as [How It Works](#how-it-works) describes.

- There is no single step that activates and runs: choose **Run** once the files are active.
- The files are handled independently: if one fails, the others carry on.
- Sodero carries on with a request after you close the page. Back on the project page, click the refresh button to follow it again.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Auto Off

**Auto off** deactivates an active file that nobody has used for 30 minutes (the default). It is on for every file unless an editor turns it off.

| File         | In use while                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Robot System | Someone has the Station open in a browser tab, or an AI agent or a Project VPN tool works with the Station |
| Robot World  | Someone watches it in **Theater**                                                                          |

Running nodes and a playing World do **not** count as use: a World left playing with no viewer is deactivated like an idle one.

When nobody is using an active file, a yellow countdown appears under its state: *Auto off in N min*. It stops when somebody opens the file, and starts a minute or two after the last person leaves.

### Turn Auto Off Off

To keep a file active on purpose, clear its **Auto off** box. The portal warns that the file is billed for every minute it stays active: click **Turn off and keep billing** to confirm, or **Keep it on**.

The warning before Auto off is turned off

The file then stays active, and keeps using credits, until somebody deactivates it. Tick the box to turn Auto off on again.

**Deactivate what you no longer need.** Auto off is a safety net, not a replacement for deactivating.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Messages and Errors

| Message                                                          | What to do                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *Activating and deactivating needs edit access to this project.* | Your role is **Can view**. Ask a manager for **Can edit**.                                                    |
| *Another Robot World is already running in this project*         | Deactivate the active World first.                                                                            |
| *This workspace has run out of credits. …*                       | See [When Credits Run Out](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/#when-credits-run-out). |
| *The … plan runs at most N Systems and Worlds at once. …*        | Deactivate another Robot System or Robot World first; stopping it is not enough.                              |
| *Environment failed to activate*                                 | Read the reason under it, then choose **Active** to try again.                                                |

# Run and Monitor

Nodes run only on the Live page, and only when you start them. This page covers starting and stopping nodes, reading their state and logs, and what to do when a node does not start.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Go Live

Open the Robot System with **Station · Edit** and click **Go live**, or activate it on the project page and open **Station · Live** ([Edit and Live](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/overview/#edit-and-live)). The Station comes up with its saved graph, documents and apps, but **no node starts by itself**: nodes that have not run yet show **Planned**.

Starting and stopping nodes needs the **Can edit** or **Can manage** role in the project.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Start All Nodes

Click **Start all nodes** in the toolbar. The Station starts every node that is not running, in dependency order: *Nodes start in dependency order: gateway → controller → compound → application.* A node waits until the nodes it requires are up.

- A banner follows the progress. **Cancel start** stops the run; nodes that already started stay up.
- The result shows as a banner: *Runtime topology is up.*, or *Runtime topology is up; stopped during startup: …* when some nodes stopped again ([When a Node Does Not Start](#6-when-a-node-does-not-start)).
- The arrow next to the button opens its menu: **Start all nodes** and **Stop all nodes**.
- *Nothing in this topology can be launched from here.* means that the graph holds only empty drafts.

**Run** on the project page does the same for a Robot System, and can start a World and several Stations in one step ([Run and Stop](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#2-run-and-stop)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Start, Restart or Stop One Node

Right-click a node on the Live page:

The menu of a running node

| Item                            | Shown when                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Open …**                      | The node has a UI of its own, for example Strider or Motion Studio                                          |
| **Start node**                  | The node is not running                                                                                     |
| **Restart node**, **Stop node** | The node runs                                                                                               |
| **Delete node**                 | Always ([Rename and Delete](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#4-rename-and-delete)) |

Start a robot's nodes in order: the gateway first, then its controller, then the nodes that use the controller. Stop them in the reverse order.

When a running app exposes its operator UI, open it from that node. See [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md) and the relevant controller chapter.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Node States

The footer of each node card and the inspector header show the node's state, and the inspector adds a short description.

| State                              | Description                              |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Planned**                        | *Not started yet.*                       |
| **Booting**, **Starting**          | *Starting up.*                           |
| **Waiting binding**                | *A required port has no connection yet.* |
| **Waiting target**                 | *Connected target is not ready yet.*     |
| **Ready**                          | *Started and waiting to operate.*        |
| **Operating**                      | *Running normally.*                      |
| **Running**, **Active**            | *Process is up.*                         |
| **Paused**                         | *Paused.*                                |
| **Idle**                           | *Instance exists but is not running.*    |
| **Degraded**                       | *Running with reduced performance.*      |
| **Disconnected**                   | *Heartbeat lost.*                        |
| **Fault**                          | *Fault state — reset to recover.*        |
| **Error**, **Failed**, **Crashed** | *The node reported an error.*            |
| **Stopped**, **Exited**            | *Process ended.*                         |

The dot next to the state is green while the node runs, yellow while it waits, red for errors and grey otherwise. Problems are also counted in the **N issues** chip of the toolbar.

**Waiting binding** means that the node runs, but a port it requires is not connected to a running node that provides it. Connect the port, and start the providing node first: the gateway before its controller. When the two ports do not fit together, the inspector shows the reason instead of the description.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Logs and Activity

On the Live page, the **Logs** section of the inspector shows the node's latest output. Choose a stream and click **Refresh**:

| Stream                                  | Contents                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Package log**                         | The app's own log                                                                                        |
| **Standard output**, **Standard error** | The program's output                                                                                     |
| **Node log (userdata)**                 | The node's log file                                                                                      |
| **Process log**                         | When the process started and stopped                                                                     |
| **Gateway events**                      | A gateway's status and problems. A controller shows the events of its gateway as **Gateway events (…)**. |

Each stream shows its last 200 lines and when it was last updated, for example *Last 200 lines · updated 5 s ago*.

- *Station packages are still being restored; this node may not start yet.* The Station is still installing its apps after going live. Wait a moment, then start the node.
- *Package restore at Station start failed: …* The node's app could not be installed ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).

**Activity**, under the logs, lists the latest changes to the node and who made them. The **Notifications** bell in the left rail lists the Station's recent events: nodes added, connected and deleted, files uploaded, and on the Live page also nodes started and stopped, and errors.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. When a Node Does Not Start

| Message                                                                                        | What to do                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| *… did not start: …*                                                                           | The app ended at once; the text after the colon is its own reason. **Details** shows more, and **Copy** copies it. Fix the cause, often the document or a setting, then start again. |
| *… cannot start yet: connect the … port or set …*                                              | The app needs that port connected, or that parameter set in **Parameters**. Do one of the two, then start again.                                                                     |
| *Install the package of … (…) from the Store first. Nothing was started.*                      | The node's app is not installed on this Station ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md))                                              |
| *Provider not ready: …* or *Requirements never bound*                                          | A node that it requires did not come up. Start that node first and read its log.                                                                                                     |
| *Process exited before reaching readiness* or *Timed out waiting for readiness*                | The node stopped or hung while starting. Read its logs.                                                                                                                              |
| *Process stopped during topology startup; check its logs before retrying.*                     | The node started, then stopped. Read its logs, fix the cause, then start again.                                                                                                      |
| *Gateway … cannot be driven by both … and …; choose one controller before starting all nodes.* | Two controllers are connected to one gateway. Disconnect one of them.                                                                                                                |
| *Project edit access is required to start or cancel the topology.*                             | Your role is **Can view**. Ask a manager for **Can edit**.                                                                                                                           |

A gateway that cannot reach its robot in the World does not fail: it waits. See [Drive Robots in the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/#7-troubleshooting).

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Stop

| To               | Do this                                                                                                                                     | The Station                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stop one node    | Right-click it › **Stop node**                                                                                                              | Stays live                                                                                |
| Stop every node  | Choose **Stop all nodes** in the menu of **Start all nodes** (users of a node stop before the node itself), or **Stop** on the project page | Stays live and keeps using credits                                                        |
| End your session | **Stop live** in the Station, or **Deactivate** on the project page                                                                         | Stops every node, saves its data and returns to the Edit page. It no longer uses credits. |

**Stop live** and **Deactivate** do the same. If nobody uses an active Station, Auto off deactivates it after 30 minutes by default ([Auto Off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off)).

Stopping this Station does not stop or deactivate its World, and does not end separate rendering sessions. End those from the project page and close unneeded views.

# Theater

Theater shows an active Robot World live in your browser: the simulation as it runs, the robots in it and the Stations that drive them. Its browser tab is titled *Cosmic Theater*.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Open Theater

1. Activate the World on the project page ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md)).
1. Click **Theater** in the World's **Actions** column. The link is available once the World is **Active** and its live view is ready.
1. In **Choose rendering mode**, pick **RTX Real-time** or **WebGPU** and click **Open Cosmic Theater** ([Choose Rendering Mode](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#choose-rendering-mode)). Theater opens in a new tab.
1. From Studio, **Enter Theater** activates the World if needed and opens it here ([Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/#7-enter-theater)).
1. While the World loads, Theater shows the progress, including **Robot cameras** when the World has cameras. The first time a scene opens in **RTX Real-time**, the renderer prepares it, which can take several minutes.
1. Opening Theater does not play the World: **Run** on the project page or **Start Theater** plays it ([Start and Stop](#start-and-stop)).
1. Watching counts as use of the World: an active World that nobody watches in Theater is deactivated by Auto off after 30 minutes.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. The Theater Window

| Area             | What it holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Header**       | The project and World names; the status, *Ready* once the World is shown; the renderer menu (**RTX Real-Time** ▾ or **WebGPU** ▾); a timer; **Start Theater** or **Stop Theater**; **Resources** ▾; **Share** (link icon); the **Active users** who are watching                   |
| **Scene assets** | The top levels of the World, with **Search assets** and the number of assets. **Hide panel** folds it away.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Viewport**     | The running World. **Perspective** ▾ holds camera presets (Perspective, Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left, Right). **View** ▾ holds **Grid**, **Quality** (resolution and frame rate), **Fit** and **Presentation mode**, which shows the viewport full screen until you press `Esc`. |
| **Readout**      | At the bottom of the viewport, for example *1920x1080 · 60 FPS · Physics RTF 1.00*                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Runtime**      | The Station that drives the selected robot ([Select a Robot](#4-select-a-robot))                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

**Physics RTF** is the real-time factor of the simulation: simulated time divided by wall-clock time, measured over about five seconds. At 1.00 the simulation keeps up with real time; *—* means there is no fresh measurement. **FPS** is the rate at which the picture is drawn.

The renderer menu switches your view to the other rendering mode. The current picture stays until the new one is ready. The choice applies to your view only; the simulation is the same for everyone.

### Start and Stop

**Start Theater** plays the World's simulation and **Stop Theater** stops it. One viewer controls them: the first person with edit access who opened Theater. For the others, the button is dimmed and they watch. Members with **Can view** always watch. While the World is not playing, viewers who watch see the status *Ready · Paused*.

Theater plays and stops only the simulation; it does not start or stop any Station. **Run** and **Stop** on the project page act on the files you select there, the World and its Stations alike ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#2-run-and-stop)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Move the Camera

The camera moves as in Studio: right-drag to look around, the wheel to move closer or farther, middle-drag to pan and `Alt` + left-drag to orbit ([Keys and Camera](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/#6-keys-and-camera)). Each viewer has their own camera.

| Key       | Action                                                                             |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `F`       | Frame the selection, or the whole World when nothing is selected                   |
| `Shift+F` | Follow the selection. A *Tracking* chip appears; **Stop** on it ends the tracking. |
| `Esc`     | Stop following; leave presentation mode                                            |

Right-click a row in **Scene assets** for **Focus** and **Focus and Track**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Select a Robot

1. Click a robot in the viewport, or its row in **Scene assets**. Double-click the row to bring the camera to the robot.
1. In **RTX Real-time**, a card appears above the robot with its name and **Open Station**, followed by the Robot System that drives it. In both modes, right-clicking the robot's row in **Scene assets** offers **Open Station** as well.
1. **Open Station** opens that Robot System's live Station in a new tab. Members with **Can view** get a page they can only look at.

The **Runtime** dock opens on the right by itself when you select a robot that a Station drives. It shows that Station's graph, read-only, with the state of each node, so you can see at a glance whether the gateway and the controller are running.

- **Widen Runtime** makes the dock wider, and **Hide Runtime** closes it. **Show Runtime** in a row's right-click menu opens it again.
- The zoom buttons and **Fit view** at the bottom arrange the graph.
- When no Station drives the robot, the card or the menu says so, for example *No Station is running in this project.*

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Several Viewers

- Everyone who opens an active World watches the same simulation. **Active users** in the header shows who is watching.
- Each person chooses their own rendering mode and moves their own camera.
- Each viewer in **RTX Real-time** has a cloud renderer of their own, which uses credits; a viewer in **WebGPU** draws with their own computer's GPU ([Credits and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)).
- **Share** shows the link to this Theater, and **Copy** copies it. The link opens for people who are signed in and have access to the project ([Share and Collaborate](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. What Theater Does Not Do

- It does not edit the World. Deactivate the World and open it in [Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md).
- It does not start or stop Stations; use **Run** and **Stop** on the project page, or the Station itself.
- It has no recording or screenshot button. To capture the view, use your operating system's screenshot or screen-recording tools.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Troubleshooting

| Message                                                          | What to do                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| *Unable to load World*, with a reason                            | Click **Retry**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| *No saved World yet*                                             | The World has no scene. Deactivate it, build the scene in Studio and save it.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| *Preparing the RTX renderer*                                     | The first time a scene opens in **RTX Real-time**, the renderer prepares it. Wait; this can take several minutes.                                                                                                                                |
| *RTX needs free GPU resources. …*                                | The cloud GPUs are busy. Wait, or close Theater and open it again in **WebGPU**.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| *The World did not finish loading in 3 minutes. …*               | The World is very large, or the renderer cannot open it. Click **Retry**; if it fails again, make the World lighter ([Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/#6-keep-the-world-light)). |
| *Physics connection failed, retrying*                            | Wait: Theater retries by itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| *Your sign-in expired. Open this World again from Sodero Cloud.* | Open Theater again from the project page.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| *No Station is running in this project.*                         | No Robot System of the project is active. Activate the one that drives the robot.                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Start Theater** is dimmed                                      | Another viewer controls the simulation, or your role is **Can view**.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| *View access: you can look but not change this project.*         | Your role is **Can view**. Ask a manager for **Can edit**.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
# Operate Robots

# Strider

Availability

These instructions apply when the required app is installed, its nodes run, and its operator UI is available. Check [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md) first.

**Strider** is the operator UI for wheeled mobile bases. With it you jog the base, watch its state and odometry, and send navigation goals. It works with every drive type that a mobile robot document (`.sddm`) can describe: differential drive, skid steer 4WD, mecanum 4WD, swerve 4WD and Ackermann.

______________________________________________________________________

## How Strider Works in a Station

Two nodes are involved:

| Node                | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sodero.mlc.<name>` | The mobile base controller. It turns body velocities into wheel commands for its gateway, integrates odometry, and keeps the speed and acceleration limits of its `.sddm` document. It has no UI of its own.                |
| `sodero.strider`    | Strider. It drives what its ports are connected to: `mobile_base` to the base controller (driving and status), `localization` to the localizer (the robot's position on the map) and `navigation` to the navigator (goals). |

```
flowchart LR
    S["sodero.strider"] -- mobile_base --> M["sodero.mlc.jackal<br>jackal.sddm"]
    M -- servo_link --> G["sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal<br>jackal.gw"]
    S -. localization .-> L["sodero.localizer"]
    S -. navigation .-> N["sodero.navigator"]
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Set Up the Nodes

1. Check that `sodero.actuator_gateway` and `sodero.mlc` are available in the Store, and select them. For Strider, also select `sodero.strider`.
1. Add the gateway and controller nodes, then connect the controller’s `servo_link` to the gateway. For Strider, connect its `mobile_base` to the base controller.
1. Go live and wait for app installation to finish. Keep the nodes stopped.
1. Upload the gateway’s `.gw` and the controller’s `.sddm` document. Reopen each node and confirm the selected document ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
1. Check the robot name and mapping, run the World, then start the gateway, controller and any dependent app.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Open Strider

If the running node provides a UI link or an **Open …** action, use it to open the app. If neither is available, check the installed app and supported version before continuing. If the session expires, reopen the UI from Station.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Screen Layout

The left rail has three pages: **Status**, **Drive** and **Navigation**. The top bar holds the actions of the current page and, on every page:

| Item             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Readiness pill   | The current state in one line, for example *Manual Drive Ready* or *Servo Off*. Click it for the checks: Connection, Mobile base, Servo, Localization, Navigation.                                 |
| **System Log**   | Events of this browser session, filtered by System, Drive, Navigation and Localization                                                                                                             |
| **Motion Alarm** | Active alarms and recent errors                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **E-STOP**       | Software stop: cancels driving and the navigation goal and sets the wheel speeds to zero at once, with the servo still on. It latches until **Clear E-Stop**, which switches the base to **Idle**. |
| Units            | `m / m/s / deg` or `m / m/s / rad`, for display only                                                                                                                                               |

### Status Page

| Card                           | Contents                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Trajectory (Odometry View)** | The path driven since the last mode change, in the odometry frame                          |
| **Operation Status**           | Ready, moving or idle, servo on or off, and faults or stops                                |
| **Base Status (Odometry)**     | Mode, and X, Y, Theta, VX, VY, WZ                                                          |
| **Control Node Health**        | Whether the base, the localizer and the navigator are reachable                            |
| **Drive Unit Status**          | The drive template and, per wheel, the servo state, position, velocity and target velocity |
| **Recent Events**              | The latest events; **View All** opens the **System Log**                                   |

**Watchdog Tripped** while the base stands still in **Twist** mode is normal: no velocity command is arriving, so the base holds zero speed.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Jog the Base

On the **Drive** page:

1. Under **Drive Mode**, click **Twist**.
1. Under **Servo / Safety**, switch **Servo On**. The readiness pill shows *Manual Drive Ready*.
1. Set the **Linear Velocity Limit** (0.2 m/s by default, at most 0.8 m/s) and the **Angular Velocity Limit**.
1. Press and hold a pad button: **Forward (W)**, **Backward (S)**, **Turn Left (A)** or **Turn Right (D)**. The base moves while you hold the button and stops when you release it; **Stop (Space)** stops it too.
1. To drive with the keyboard, switch on **Live** in **Manual Drive**, then use **W**, **S**, **A**, **D** and **Space**. Commands stop when the window loses focus.
1. When you are done, switch the servo off and click **Idle**.

| Control                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Drive Mode**         | **Idle**: no motion. **Twist**: body velocity commands, for jogging and navigation. **Wheel**: direct wheel speeds (advanced). **EMG**: stops the base like **E-STOP**, without latching. |
| **Servo On** / **Off** | Enables or disables the drives. **Fault Reset** clears drive faults; then switch the servo off and on again.                                                                              |
| **Stop Motion**        | Stops manual driving and cancels a navigation goal                                                                                                                                        |

Manual commands take priority over navigation: jogging during a navigation goal overrides the navigator and can end the goal. A manual command expires after about a second, so the base stops if the connection drops. A navigation goal does not expire: cancel it with **Stop Motion**, **Cancel** or **E-STOP**.

**Show** next to **Advanced Controls** opens **Wheel Direct** (each wheel's speed in **Wheel** mode), **Preview Command** (the wheel speeds a body velocity would give, without moving), **Steering Origin**, **Calibration** and **Record / Replay**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Navigation Page

The **Navigation** page works when Strider's `localization` and `navigation` ports are connected to a running localizer and navigator, and the Station has a map bundle ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/#2-kinds-of-documents)).

| Card                                                                         | Contents                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Navigation Map (Occupancy Grid)**                                          | The map, the robot, the planned path and the goal. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.                                       |
| **Localization Status**                                                      | Healthy, Degraded, Initializing, Relocalizing, Lost or Uninitialized. **Global localization** searches the whole map. |
| **Mission Status**, **Current Pose (Map)**, **Goal Pose**, **Route Summary** | The goal, where the robot is and how far it still has to go                                                           |
| **Navigator**                                                                | The navigator's state and a **Speed Limit** slider (10–100 %)                                                         |
| **Navigation Controls**                                                      | **Set Initial Pose**, **Set Goal**, **Clear Goal**, **Pause**, **Resume**, **Cancel**                                 |

### Set the Initial Pose

If the localization status is not **Healthy**:

1. Click **Set Initial Pose**.
1. Press on the map where the robot stands and drag in the direction it faces.
1. Click **Set initial pose** (or **Relocalize here** when a pose was set before).

### Send a Goal

1. Make sure the base is in **Twist** with the servo on: the readiness pill shows *Navigation Ready*.
1. Click **Set Goal**, press on the map where the robot should go and drag in the direction it should face.
1. Click **Start Navigation**. The planned path appears.

**Pause** cancels the goal and keeps it; **Resume** sends it again. **Cancel** stops navigation.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Control Strider from Programs

- **AI agents** drive the base with the `strider` tools: state, servo, velocities, stops and fault reset ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md)).
- **Your own module** on the Station connects to the base controller's `mobile_base` port ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).
- **Your own tools** on your computer reach the Station API through the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md).

# Motion Studio

Availability

These instructions apply when the required app is installed, its nodes run, and its operator UI is available. Check [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md) first.

**Motion Studio** is the operator UI for manipulators. The manipulator controller node, `sodero.mmc.<name>`, runs the arm's real-time controller: kinematics, dynamics, trajectory generation and safety limits, from the arm's `.sdd` document. Motion Studio belongs to that node. It shows the arm in 3D, jogs it, defines tools and teaches poses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Set Up the Nodes

1. Check that `sodero.actuator_gateway` and `sodero.mmc` are available in the Store, and select them.
1. Add the gateway and controller nodes, then connect the controller’s `servo_link` to the gateway.
1. Go live and wait for app installation to finish. Keep the nodes stopped.
1. Upload the gateway’s `.gw` and the controller’s `.sdd` document. Reopen each node and confirm the selected document ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
1. Check the robot name and mapping, run the World, then start the gateway, controller and any dependent app.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Open Motion Studio

If the running node provides a UI link or an **Open …** action, use it to open the app. If neither is available, check the installed app and supported version before continuing. If the session expires, reopen the UI from Station.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Screen Layout

| Item                   | Description                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pages                  | **Home**, **Tool** and **Pose**                                                              |
| 3D view                | The arm in its current pose, with the 3D model of its `.sdd`                                 |
| **Joint Status**       | Per joint: position, target position, velocity, target velocity, effort and residual effort  |
| **TCP Status**         | Position and orientation of the tool center point (TCP), and its linear and angular velocity |
| **Active Tool Status** | The active tool's TCP offset, center of mass and payload mass                                |
| **Filters**            | Shows or hides the cards of the Home page                                                    |

### Header

| Item                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Robot and role        | The controller node, and whether this window has control (*Pilot - Control Active*)                                                                                                                                         |
| **Manual** / **Auto** | **Manual** limits the linear speed of the TCP in the controller's own motions and jogs, 0.25 m/s by default; it does not limit rotations or **Hand** mode. **Auto** runs at the programmed speed.                           |
| Feed rate             | Speed override in percent (10–150 %), applied to motion in progress                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Error Reset**       | Clears a protective stop (a joint at its limit, a speed or torque limit, a detected collision) and resets drive faults. Switch the servo on again afterwards. If the arm stays stopped, stop and start its controller node. |
| Units                 | `mm / g / deg` or `m / kg / radian`                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Jog**               | Opens the jog panel                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Command log**       | Commands sent from this window                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Alarm**             | Active alarms and notifications                                                                                                                                                                                             |

The mark at the top left opens the menu, with **File** to import and export tools and poses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Jog the Arm

Click **Jog** in the header to open the jog panel.

1. Switch **Servo On**.
1. In **JOG OPTION**, choose the **Mode**:
   - **Joint**: move one joint at a time (J1…Jn).
   - **Base**: move the tool in the robot's base frame (X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ).
   - **Tool**: move the tool in its own frame.
   - **Hand**: hand guiding, for a real arm. The arm compensates gravity and the jog buttons are disabled.
1. Choose **Continuous** (moves while you hold a button) or **Step** (5° or 10 mm per click), and the **Speed**: 50 %, 100 % or 150 %, about 0.04, 0.1 and 0.2 m/s at the tool.
1. Hold **−** or **+** next to a joint or axis in **JOG CONTROL**. The motion stops when you release the button.

The **POSE** section of the panel shows the current TCP pose and joint positions.

**Stop motion explicitly before leaving the UI.** A continuous jog depends on delivery of the button-release command. If the browser or connection fails, do not assume motion has stopped. Stop the controller from Station and confirm the robot has stopped in Theater. For physical robots, follow the hardware stop procedure in the Stellar X manual.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Tools

The **Tool** page defines the tools mounted on the flange.

1. Click **+** to add a tool, and rename it with the pencil icon, for example `gripper`.
1. Enter the **TOOL CENTER POINT**: the TCP position and orientation relative to the flange. The calculator icon opens **TCP Calibration**, which computes the TCP from 3–10 poses that touch the same point.
1. Enter the **PAYLOAD PROPERTIES**: center of mass, inertia and mass. The calculator icon opens **Payload Calibration**.
1. Click **Save**, or **Save and Apply** to make it the active tool at once. **Set as active tool** activates a saved tool.

A wrong payload makes hand guiding and collision detection unreliable. Set the mass and center of mass of every tool you mount.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Poses

The **Pose** page stores named poses.

1. Jog the arm to the pose, then click the camera icon (**Save Current Pose**). Or click **+** (**Add pose**) and fill in the values.
1. Select the pose in the list. **POSE DATA** shows its TCP pose and joint positions; **Set from current** copies the current pose into it.
1. Under **TEST MOVE**, choose **Joint** or **Linear** motion and hold **Hold to move**. The arm moves to the pose only while you hold the button.
1. Click **Save**.

Saved poses appear as markers in the 3D view. Right-click a pose to copy, duplicate or delete it. **File** in the menu exports and imports tools and poses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Program the Arm

Motion Studio is for setup and teaching. Programs run outside it and use the same controller:

| From            | How                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AI agents       | The `motion` tools: state, servo, moves, stops and fault reset ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md))                |
| Your own module | A module node on the Station, connected to the manipulator controller node ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)) |
| Your own tools  | The Station API, through the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md)                                                |

**From simulation to a real arm.** The arm's `.sdd` document, its tools and poses, and your programs carry over to a real arm on Stellar X, which uses an EtherCAT gateway instead of the simulation gateway. A real arm needs its own checks first: see [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/controllers/motion_studio/) in the Stellar X manual.

# Articulation

Availability

These instructions apply when the required app is installed, its nodes run, and its operator UI is available. Check [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md) first.

The **Articulation** controller drives an articulated robot joint by joint: legged robots, humanoids, grippers, pan-tilt heads, or any set of joints that receives joint targets. Unlike the manipulator controller, it uses no arm kinematics (no DH parameters, no Cartesian motions). It bounds and forwards the joint targets of an upper controller, such as a walking policy in your own module, and its **Articulation** UI lets you jog the joints by hand.

| Item     | Value                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node     | `sodero.amc.<name>`                                                                                                                                               |
| Document | `.sdda`, made in Stellar Designer ([Articulated Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/tutorials/stellar_designer/articulation/) in the Stellar X manual) |
| Joints   | 1 to 64, driven by one actuator gateway                                                                                                                           |
| Units    | rad, rad/s, N·m                                                                                                                                                   |

```
flowchart LR
    U["Upper controller<br>your module"] -- "joint targets" --> A["Articulation<br>sodero.amc.dog"]
    A -- servo_link --> G["Actuator gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.dog"]
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. The Document

An `.sdda` document lists the joints and how the gateway's actuators drive them.

| Per joint          | Meaning                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name               | Joint name                                                 |
| Position min / max | Range of motion; targets outside it are refused            |
| Velocity max       | Velocity limit, also the reference for the jog speed       |
| Torque max         | Torque limit; the controller clamps its total output to it |
| Offset (optional)  | Joint position at actuator position zero                   |
| Kp, Kd (optional)  | Stiffness and damping, for PD torque control               |

- **Drive mode.** In `position` mode, the controller bounds the joint targets and the drive follows them with its own position control. In `pd_torque` mode, the controller computes a PD torque from Kp and Kd and sends torque commands.
- **Actuator mapping.** One actuator can move several joints, and several actuators can move one joint, as long as the mapping can be inverted.
- **Watchdogs.** The controller switches the servo off and latches a stop when the gateway's feedback is older than 100 ms, or when no new target arrives for 200 ms (the defaults). Click **Clear stop**, then **Servo on**. Reconnecting never switches the servo on by itself.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Set Up the Nodes

1. Check that `sodero.actuator_gateway` and `sodero.amc` are available in the Store, and select them.
1. Add the gateway and controller nodes, then connect the controller’s `servo_link` to the gateway.
1. Go live and wait for app installation to finish. Keep the nodes stopped.
1. Upload the gateway’s `.gw` and the controller’s `.sdda` document. Reopen each node and confirm the selected document ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
1. Check the robot name and mapping, run the World, then start the gateway, controller and any dependent app.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Open the Articulation UI

If the running node provides a UI link or an **Open …** action, use it to open the app. If neither is available, check the installed app and supported version before continuing. If the session expires, reopen the UI from Station.

| Area              | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Left rail         | **Joints** (joint monitor), **Constraints** (the configured limits), **Set origin**                                                                                                                             |
| Top bar           | **Servo on**, **Servo off**, **Stop** (switches the servo off and latches a stop), **Clear stop** (releases it while the servo is off), the control mode, and the button that opens the **Joint control** panel |
| Status strip      | **Servo** on or off, **Feedback** age in milliseconds, **Safety** (*Ready* or the reason for a stop)                                                                                                            |
| **Controller**    | The Articulation node this window controls                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Joint monitor** | Per joint: position, velocity, effort and target                                                                                                                                                                |

**Stop the upper controller first.** Pause or stop the program that sends joint targets, such as a walking policy, before you jog the joints by hand.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Jog Joints

1. Open the **Joint control** panel with the button at the right of the top bar.
1. Click **Servo on**.
1. Under **Joint jog**, set the **Speed**: 1–100 % of each joint's velocity limit, 10 % by default.
1. Hold **−** or **+** next to a joint. The joint moves while you hold the button and holds its position when you release it. A jog button also switches the servo on if it is off.

Leaving the window, switching to another tab or losing the connection switches the servo off.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Send Joint Targets

Under **Joint targets**:

1. Click **Use measured positions** to copy the current positions into the target fields.
1. Change the targets of the joints you want to move.
1. Click **Stream targets**. The controller follows the targets while the stream runs; **Stop target stream** ends it and switches the servo off.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Set the Origin

**Set origin** gives the current position of a joint a known angle, for example after an encoder was replaced on a real robot. Robots in a Robot World do not support it. For real robots, see [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/controllers/articulation/) in the Stellar X manual.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Control from Programs

| From            | How                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A walking robot | Your module runs the walking policy and sends joint targets to the Articulation node                                                                      |
| AI agents       | The `articulation` tools: state, servo, moves, stops and fault reset ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md)) |
| Your own tools  | The Station API, through the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md)                                       |
# Connect and Automate

# Project VPN

Availability

Continue only if the **Project VPN** panel provides an installer for your operating system and your project role allows a connection. If no installer is available, contact Sodero. The installed release determines the exact approval prompts.

The Project VPN connects your own computer to the Stations of a project, so you can use a Station's API from a terminal, your own scripts or your IDE. You approve every connection yourself, and a connection lasts at most 8 hours.

**AI agents don't need the Project VPN.** To work on a project with Claude Code or another AI agent, see [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## What the Project VPN Reaches

A connection reaches one thing: the **Station API on port 8001** of each Station (Robot System) that was active when you connected. It does not reach other ports, Robot Worlds, Stations activated or restarted after you connected, or other projects. Your computer can call a Station, but a Station cannot connect to your computer.

The Project VPN doesn't start anything: activate the Stations you want to use first ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md)). An active Station uses credits whether or not you are connected, and your tools' calls to it count as use for [Auto off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off).

People who can manage the project (and, where enabled, editors) can connect computers and copy Station API keys. Others see *Your project role can't use the Project VPN. Ask the project owner for access.*

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Install the Sodero VPN Toolkit

Install the toolkit once on each computer you want to connect. The portal calls the installed program **SoderoConnector**; your system lists it as **Sodero VPN**.

1. Open the project and click **Project VPN** in the top bar.
1. In the **This PC** row, under **Install the Sodero VPN toolkit**, the panel shows the install command for your computer. Copy it from there with **Copy**.
1. Run the command: on Linux or macOS in a terminal, as your normal user; on Windows in PowerShell. Approve the administrator prompt.

The Project VPN panel of Warehouse Demo

**No install command?** If the panel says *A pinned toolkit installer has not been published on this server yet.*, the Project VPN cannot be set up yet. Contact Sodero.

On Linux, the installer supports Debian and Ubuntu. On Windows, it also installs WireGuard for Windows, which Sodero VPN uses.

The toolkit also adds the `sodero` command and an optional status icon (**Sodero VPN** in your app menu, or `sodero tray`).

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Connect This Computer

1. Activate at least one Station of the project. In **Project VPN**, click **Connect this PC**.
1. Your browser asks whether to open SoderoConnector. Allow it.
1. The connection window **Sodero — connect and approve** opens. If it asks you to sign in, sign in with your Sodero account in the browser tab that opens.
1. SoderoConnector shows the project, this computer's name and a six-character **Confirmation code**. Check the project, then approve as the prompts ask: type the code in SoderoConnector, or check that the portal shows the same code, tick the box and click **Approve this device**. When both sides ask, do both.
1. The row shows **Connected**. **Details** lists the Stations in this connection.

**Approve only a connection you started.** If a confirmation code appears that you didn't expect, cancel the request and don't approve it.

**Keep SoderoConnector running.** The connection stays open only while the program that made it runs: the connection window, or the terminal command. Once the portal says *The device manages this connection; the browser can close.*, you can close the portal tab.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Connect from a Terminal

You can connect without the portal page, for example on a computer you reach over SSH:

```
sodero login                                # once: sign in through your browser
sodero vpn connect --project PROJECT_ID     # stays in the foreground
```

1. `sodero login` opens the Sodero sign-in in your browser. Without a desktop, it prints the sign-in address and explains how to open it; finish within 5 minutes.
1. Replace `PROJECT_ID` with the project's identifier: in the project, open **AI agents** and expand **Advanced: project identifier**.
1. Answer `y` to *Connect this device to this project? [y/N]*, then type the **Confirmation code** that the command prints.
1. Leave the command running: `Ctrl+C` or closing the terminal disconnects. To keep the connection after you log out of SSH, run it inside `tmux` or `screen`.

`sodero vpn status` shows the connection, `sodero vpn disconnect` ends it, and `sodero --help` lists all commands.

This `sodero` command belongs to the Sodero VPN toolkit. It is not the [sodero CLI](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/ssh_workspace/sodero_cli/) of the Stellar X SSH workspace.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Connect Another Device

**Connect another device** connects a different computer, for example a Linux machine without a desktop.

1. In **Project VPN**, click **Connect another device** and choose **CLI terminal** or **Desktop app**.
1. On the device, install the toolkit with the command shown in the row.
1. **CLI terminal:** run `sodero login` with the same Sodero account, then the connect command from the row, and keep it running. **Desktop app:** paste the link from the row into the device's browser.
1. Approve with the confirmation code, as in [step 2](#2-connect-this-computer).

The link works once, for one device, and only for 60 seconds; **Get a new link** makes a new one. The device must connect within 5 minutes.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Use a Station's Address and API Key

Each Station has its own address on the Project VPN. It stays the same when the Station is deactivated and activated again. You find it in **Station addresses** in the **Project VPN** panel and in the **IP address** column of the project's Robot Systems.

1. Connect this computer while the Station is active.
1. Click the copy icon next to the Station's address. It copies `http://ADDRESS:8001/`.
1. In **Station addresses**, click the key icon (*Copy the Station's API key*). The key is copied to your clipboard; it is never shown on screen.
1. In your tools, use the address and send the key with each request. The message that confirms the copy names the request header to use.

**The key changes each time the Station starts.** After the Station is deactivated and activated again, connect again and copy the new key.

**Keep the key private.** Treat it like a password: don't paste it into shared documents and don't commit it with your code.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Disconnect

Click **Disconnect** in the portal, **Disconnect and close window** in the connection window or **Disconnect VPN** in the status icon. In a terminal, press `Ctrl+C` where `sodero vpn connect` runs, or run `sodero vpn disconnect`.

A connection also ends on its own after 8 hours; about a minute after the program that holds it stops, for example when the computer sleeps; when all its Stations are deactivated or restarted; when you lose access to the project; or when your workspace has used its Project VPN time or data for the month. The toolkit never reconnects on its own.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Update or Uninstall the Toolkit

To update, run the install command from the panel with `update` in place of `install`, then connect again. To uninstall, run `sodero uninstall` (add `--purge` to also remove the VPN settings and the device identity), or on Windows uninstall **Sodero VPN** in **Installed apps**. WireGuard for Windows stays installed.

______________________________________________________________________

## Limits

| What                        | Limit                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Open connections per person | 3, across all your projects                                  |
| Connections per computer    | 1 at a time                                                  |
| Length of a connection      | 8 hours                                                      |
| Monthly use                 | Project VPN time and data per workspace, as your plan allows |

**Billing & Usage** shows the Project VPN time and data used this month ([Credits and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)). When they are used up, new connections are refused until the counters reset.

______________________________________________________________________

## Troubleshooting

| Message or symptom                                                | What to do                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *No running Station is available for this project.*               | Activate at least one Station, then connect.                                                                                                                                                   |
| *You have 3 connections, the maximum. …*                          | Disconnect a connection you don't need, here or in another project.                                                                                                                            |
| *No response from SoderoConnector. …*                             | Install or start the toolkit, allow your browser to open it, then click **Open SoderoConnector again**. If this computer is connected from another tab, click **Use here** on that connection. |
| A Station is missing, or *Some Stations stopped or changed. …*    | The Station was activated or restarted after you connected. Disconnect, then connect again.                                                                                                    |
