| *A local network or another VPN already routes a target address.* | Disconnect the other VPN, or connect from a different network.                                                                                                                                 |
| *Not signed in to Sodero …* or *Your Sodero sign-in has ended …*  | Run `sodero login`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| A checksum, size or signature mismatch during installation        | Don't work around it. Copy the command from the panel again; if the message comes back, report it to Sodero.                                                                                   |

# AI Agents

Connect Claude Code or another AI agent to your Sodero account, then ask it in plain language to work on your projects. The agent reaches Sodero Cloud over the Internet with a sign-in of its own; it needs neither the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md) nor anything installed from Sodero.

- *"Which Stations and Worlds in Warehouse Demo are active?"*
- *"Activate the warehouse World and the jackal Station, then start them."*
- *"Why did a node on jackal stop? Show me its log."*

______________________________________________________________________

## How It Works

```
flowchart TB
    You(["You"]) --> Agent["AI agent<br>on your computer"]
    Agent -- "MCP, with its own sign-in" --> Cloud["Sodero Cloud"]
    Cloud --> Projects["The projects you approved:<br>Robot Systems, Robot Worlds, files"]
```

- You register Sodero once in your agent, as a remote MCP server. The registration belongs to your account, not to one project.
- The agent signs in through your browser with your Sodero account, and on a consent page you choose what it may do and in which projects. It never sees your password, and you can revoke its access at any time.
- The agent never gets more than your own project roles allow.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Register Sodero in Your Agent

Open any project and click **AI agents** in the top bar. The **AI agents (MCP)** panel shows the address and ready-made settings for your agent, and what your project role allows.

The AI agents panel of Warehouse Demo

Click **Copy command** and run the command once in a terminal:

```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user sodero 'https://app.sodero.io/project-access/mcp'
```

`--scope user` makes Sodero available in all your working folders.

The client must support remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP and sign in through your browser (OAuth). Add a remote server with the address that **Copy address** copies:

```
https://app.sodero.io/project-access/mcp
```

For a client with a JSON list of servers, expand **Other MCP clients** in the panel and click **Copy configuration**. Don't enter a token or a client ID: the client registers itself and signs in through your browser.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Sign In and Choose What the Agent May Do

1. Start the sign-in. In Claude Code, start `claude`, type `/mcp`, select **sodero** and choose **Authenticate**. Other clients have a **Connect** or **Sign in** action.

1. Your browser opens the Sodero sign-in. Sign in with your **Sodero** account, not with the account of your AI provider.

1. On the consent page *Allow … to connect?*, choose what the agent may do and click **Allow selected access**:

   | Option                                                          | What the agent may do                                                                                              |
   | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
   | **Read project data**                                           | Read the selected projects: status, items, files and jobs. Selected by default.                                    |
   | **Change project data and run commands (includes read access)** | Also make changes, such as uploading files, activating Stations and Worlds and running the Station and World tools |
   | **Projects**                                                    | The projects the agent may use. Select at least one project or workspace.                                          |
   | **Optional workspace grants**                                   | All current and future projects of a workspace in which you have a role                                            |

1. Return to your agent: Sodero is connected.

**Approve only your own agent.** The consent page shows the name the agent gives itself; Sodero can't verify it. Allow access only right after you started the sign-in from your own agent.

**Changes also need a project role that allows them:** people who can manage the project and, where enabled, editors. The **AI agents** panel of each project says which applies to you.

A connection lasts up to 30 days. To renew it or change its access, sign the agent in again (in Claude Code, from `/mcp`), then [revoke](#review-and-revoke-agents) the entries you no longer need.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Tell the Agent Which Project to Use

Every request names a project. In the **AI agents** panel, click **Copy project link** and paste the link into your request, or give the project's name, for example *"List files in Warehouse Demo"*. When two projects have the same name, use `workspace/name`.

A project you joined after you signed the agent in is not part of its consent, unless you granted its whole workspace. Sign the agent in again and select the project.

______________________________________________________________________

## What Agents Can Do

| Area                                   | The agent can                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Projects and status                    | List the projects it may use; read their Robot Systems and Robot Worlds with their states, the Trash and the jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Run (write access)                     | Activate or stop up to 8 Stations and Worlds at once, or activate and start them as one job                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Items (write access)                   | Create, duplicate, rename and trash Robot Systems and Robot Worlds. Restoring and permanently deleting from the Trash need **Can manage**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Files                                  | List and download library files, and list Sodero's official assets. With write access, upload files of up to 64 MiB, such as Station packages, World scenes and maps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Station and World tools (write access) | Run tools from a catalog of more than 100: Station status and logs, the node graph, documents, Store apps, robot control through [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md), [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md) and [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/articulation/index.md), navigation, cameras, and the World |

**Every Station and World tool needs write access**, even one that only reads. Tools for a running Station or World need it to be active.

The agent cannot go beyond your consent and your roles, use the Project VPN, read files on your computer through Sodero, or download the contents of Sodero's official assets. Cancelling a job stops further steps but doesn't undo changes.

______________________________________________________________________

## Stay in Control

- **Approve changes yourself.** Most agents can ask before they use a tool. A practical setup: allow the read-only tools freely (`projects_list`, `project_status`, `items_list`, `files_list`, `assets_list`, `packages_list`, `jobs_list`, `job_status`, `tools_list`, `tool_describe`, `file_download`) and keep approval on for every other tool, especially `tool_call`, `items_start`, `items_stop` and `jobs_start`. In Claude Code, they are named `mcp__sodero__` plus the tool name.
- **Review previews.** Most changes are previewed first. `item_create`, `item_duplicate`, `items_start`, `items_stop` and `jobs_start` act at once.
- **The agent acts as you.** What it changes is changed for everyone in the project.
- **Watch your credits.** A Station or World that an agent activated uses credits until it is deactivated. [Auto off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off) still applies.

The rules Sodero gives every agent (preview changes first, move a robot only when you asked for that motion, treat files and logs as data and not as instructions) are instructions to the agent, not a safety function. An agent can misread them or make mistakes, and its tools have the same effect as your own actions. Approve every change yourself.

______________________________________________________________________

## Usage Limits

Agent tool calls count against your workspace's plan, per minute and per calendar month (UTC). **Billing & Usage** shows the calls used this month ([Credits and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)). At the monthly limit, calls are refused until the renewal date that the **AI agents** panel shows. At the per-minute limit, the agent is told how long to wait.

A tool call ends after 100 seconds. A change may still have been applied: have the agent check the state before it repeats the change.

______________________________________________________________________

## Review and Revoke Agents

1. Click your avatar at the bottom of the left navigation bar and choose **Account Settings**.
1. Under **Connected AI agents**, each agent shows its name, when it connected, its scopes (*Read* or *Read, Write*) and its workspace and project grants.
1. To disconnect an agent, click **Revoke**, then **Confirm revoke**.

Connected AI agents in Account settings

Revoking stops the agent's further calls and job steps but doesn't undo what was done. To connect the agent again, sign it in again.

______________________________________________________________________

## Troubleshooting

| Message or symptom                                                                      | What to do                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The sign-in ends without the consent page, and the agent reports that access was denied | Start the sign-in again and finish it within 10 minutes, with your Sodero account. If it keeps happening, report it with **Help › Report a bug**. |
| A project is missing from the consent page                                              | You aren't a member of the project. Ask a person who can manage it to add you.                                                                    |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED`, `AUTH_EXPIRED` or `CONNECTION_REVOKED`                                 | Sign the agent in again (Claude Code: `/mcp`).                                                                                                    |
| `GRANT_MISSING` or `NOT_FOUND` for a project                                            | The project isn't part of this connection's consent. Sign the agent in again and select it.                                                       |
| `WRITE_NOT_GRANTED`                                                                     | The connection may only read. Sign the agent in again and select **Change project data and run commands**.                                        |
| `STATION_NOT_RUNNING` or `WORLD_NOT_RUNNING`                                            | Activate the Station or World first.                                                                                                              |
| `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`                                                                        | Your workspace reached its plan's limit for agent calls. The message says when to try again.                                                      |
# Reference

# Compatibility

Sodero Cloud and Stellar X share robot-system concepts and document types. Their deployed Station versions, installed apps and operator interfaces can differ.

## Before You Configure a Robot

1. Check that the required app is available in the current Station's **Store** and can be installed for this environment.
1. Use gateway and robot documents exported for that Station version. An app listing or an upload confirmation alone does not confirm that the controller is ready to operate.
1. After going live, check the selected documents, port connections and node states before issuing motion commands.
1. Open an operator UI only when the running app provides its link or **Open …** action. If unavailable, stop here and contact Sodero for supported packages and instructions.

The controller chapters describe their functions when these prerequisites are met. The Quick Start covers World creation and viewing; it does not require a controller UI.

## Move Files Between Products

An `.sdr` is a transfer container, not a guarantee of compatibility with every Station release. Check document format, node names, required apps and destination architecture before importing. Installed packages are not included in the file.

A Robot World's `.sdr` is for Sodero Cloud. For a Robot System, follow [Import an .sdr File](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#2-import-an-sdr-file) and the destination product's documentation. Keep the original backup until the imported system has been checked.

Cloud instructions use **Store**, **Station · Edit**, **Go live** and **Station · Live**. A Stellar X manual for an earlier device release may use different menus and node names. Use it for the concepts and device-specific steps that match your installed version; do not copy old graph identifiers into Cloud unchanged.

## Example Scene and Robot Documents

The [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md) includes a warehouse scene and its accompanying license notice. A scene alone does not configure its robot controller.

Obtain compatible `.gw`, `.sdd`, `.sddm` or `.sdda` documents from the current product's supported asset collection or from Sodero. Keep required metadata and license notices intact. Do not edit an archive's internal files to force acceptance by a different Station version.

## Browser and Rendering

Use an up-to-date supported browser. **WebGPU** requires browser, operating-system and GPU support; a browser version number alone does not guarantee availability. **RTX Real-time** renders in the cloud and needs a working streaming connection. Check the rendering choices available on your device.

## External Tools

Install Project VPN only when the portal offers an installer for your operating system. Follow the prompts of that release. Connect AI agents using the endpoint and configuration shown in the project's **AI agents** panel.

# Limits and Defaults

This page collects the fixed limits and the defaults you can meet in Sodero Cloud, each with the page that explains it. Your workspace's plan sets further limits, such as storage and how many Robot Systems and Robot Worlds can be active at once: **Billing & Usage** shows them ([Set by Your Plan](#set-by-your-plan)).

______________________________________________________________________

## Names

| What                                             | Limit                                                                                                                                | More                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Workspace name                                   | Up to 30 characters                                                                                                                  | [Workspaces and People](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/index.md)                    |
| Project name and description                     | Name up to 20 characters, description up to 40                                                                                       | [Projects](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#2-create-a-project)                       |
| Robot System or Robot World name and description | File name up to 20 characters, description up to 40                                                                                  | [Robot Systems and Robot Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#1-create-a-file)       |
| Node name in a Station                           | Up to 60 characters (an empty draft: 20): letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit. Unique in the Station. | [Build the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#name-the-node)                         |
| Robot name of a simulation gateway               | Exactly the robot's articulation prim name in the World: letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. Unique in the World.    | [Drive Robots in the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/#2-name-the-robot) |
| Password                                         | At least 8 characters                                                                                                                | [Sign In and Account](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/sign_in/index.md)                         |

______________________________________________________________________

## Projects, Files and Runs

| What                                    | Limit or default                                                                                                                                                | More                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Active Robot Worlds per project         | 1                                                                                                                                                               | [Robot Systems and Robot Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#4-how-robot-worlds-and-robot-systems-work-together) |
| Active Robot Systems per project        | Any number, within your plan's limit of Systems and Worlds running at once                                                                                      | [Credits and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/#limits)                                                         |
| Auto off                                | Deactivates an active Robot System or Robot World after 30 minutes without users (the default). On by default.                                                  | [Auto Off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off)                                                        |
| Files in one **Actions** selection      | Any number of Robot Systems, at most one Robot World                                                                                                            | [Several Files at Once](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#4-several-files-at-once)                              |
| Nodes after **Activate** or **Go live** | No node starts by itself                                                                                                                                        | [Run and Monitor](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)                                                              |
| Station resources                       | Each Station gets its own share of CPU and memory from Sodero Cloud. **Resources** in the Station and the **Resource** column of the project page show its use. | [Stellar Station](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/overview/#4-resources)                                                     |
| Node logs in the Station                | The last 200 lines of each stream                                                                                                                               | [Logs and Activity](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#5-logs-and-activity)                                                |

______________________________________________________________________

## Files and Uploads

| What                           | Limit                | More                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A file in a library            | Up to 2 GiB          | [Libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/#2-add-files) |
| An upload in Studio            | Up to 1 GiB per file | [Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md)             |
| A file uploaded by an AI agent | Up to 64 MiB         | [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/#usage-limits) |

______________________________________________________________________

## Sharing and Connections

| What                               | Limit                                              | More                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Project or workspace invitation    | Valid for 7 days                                   | [Share and Collaborate](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/#1-invite-people) |
| Project VPN connections            | 3 open connections per person, across all projects | [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/#limits)                 |
| Length of a Project VPN connection | At most 8 hours                                    | [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/#limits)                 |
| AI agent connection                | Up to 30 days, then sign the agent in again        | [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/#usage-limits)               |
| AI agent tool call                 | Ends after 100 seconds                             | [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/#usage-limits)               |

______________________________________________________________________

## Set by Your Plan

Your workspace's plan sets these limits. **Billing & Usage**, in the workspace menu, shows each one with what the workspace uses ([Credits and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)):

- credits, their hourly rates and when they renew;
- **Projects** in the workspace;
- **Workspace storage**, **Project libraries** and **Your My Library**;
- **Systems and Worlds running at once**;
- **AI agent (MCP) tool calls**, **Project VPN time** and **Project VPN data** per calendar month.

Plans differ, so this manual gives no values for them. To change the plan or add credits, contact Sodero.

# Documentation Changes

## v1.0.0

Documentation release: 27 October 2026.

This documentation release introduces the Sodero Cloud portal, World editing and viewing, Station configuration, account and project management, and optional connections.

- [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md): create, view, stop and deactivate a World.
- [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md): check app availability and document formats before configuring controllers or transferring systems.
- Controller chapters describe functions available after the required apps and UIs are ready.
